"King, even the wild beasts of prey show respect to my dwelling place. Why did you kill the deer that came here for refuge?" When the hermit spoke these words to the king, the royal troops arrived and asked, "Lord, who is this person speaking to?" The king replied, "He is speaking to me." They said, "O wise ones, what is the punishment for one who speaks harshly to the king?" They answered, "Lord, the punishment for that is death." "If that is the case," the king said, "then I fully abandon this hermit."

As they prepared to kill him, and while he was being executed, the hermit made a perverted prayer <note>original: "smon lam log par btab pa," an aspiration made with malicious intent</note>: "Since this quarrelsome king is killing me though I am innocent and have done no harm, wherever he is reborn, may I be the one to deprive him of his life." Then he thought further: "These kings are extremely well-guarded, well-protected, and well-watched. If I take rebirth elsewhere, I might never find an opportunity. Therefore, by this prayer, may I be reborn in the womb of his chief queen."

Due to that perverted prayer, he was conceived in the womb of Queen Gochen <note>original: "Gos can," meaning "Clothed One"</note>. On the very day of his conception, a rain of blood fell. Queen Gochen then developed a strange pregnancy craving: "Oh, if only I could cut and eat the flesh from the king's back!" When this was reported to the king, he summoned the diviners and questioned them.

<leaf-break/>

"He will become <note>the context implies a prediction of the future child's actions</note>." The king thought, "If he is going to deprive me of life for the sake of the kingdom, then if I give him the kingdom myself, why would he take my life?"

At that time, in the city of Vaishali <note>original: "Yangs pa can"</note>, there lived a prominent Licchavi named Mingchen <note>original: "Ming chen," meaning "Great Name"</note>. In his pleasure grove, there was a mango grove where a plantain tree <note>a banana tree</note> suddenly grew. The keeper of the grove saw it. Immediately, flowers began to bloom on it. Amazed, he told Mingchen, who then summoned and questioned the diviners.

They said, "Lord, please guard this tree. On the seventh day, it will burst open, and a girl will emerge from within it." When the householder Mingchen heard this, he was even more amazed. He stationed guards all around the pleasure grove and began counting the days. When the seven days had passed, he had the grove cleared of stones, pebbles, and debris. He had the ground sprinkled with sandalwood water, set out fragrant incense burners, hung many silk tassels, and scattered loose flowers. Arise! The assembly of the deities of the <term>Yangdak</term> <gloss>Pure/Authentic</gloss> Mind, who possess the sacred bond; may the fifty-eight primary and subordinate deities arise from the basic space! From the unmanifest basic space, please come to this place! Remain firmly in the place of the <term>samaya</term> <gloss>sacred bond</gloss> mandala! I offer non-dual prostrations and offerings. Accept this offering of the <term>amrita</term> <gloss>nectar</gloss> of sacred substances! Stir your sacred bond and perform the requested activities! The invocation of the assembly of deities of <term>Manjushri</term>'s <gloss>the Bodhisattva of Wisdom</gloss> Body is as follows: <term>Hum</term>! From the great mandala of the Play of the Lord of Death, may the assembly of deities of <term>Manjushri</term>'s Body arise from the basic space! From the central hub of the mandala: the Great Glorious Bhagavan <term>Yamantaka</term> <gloss>Slayer of Death</gloss>, the Father.
<leaf-break/>
The unique Father, the Great Slayer who Subdues Darkness; and the unique Mother, the Black One with a Single Braid. The unique Father, the Lord of Death <term>Phyasang</term>; and the unique Mother, the Crystal Nine-Faced One. The unique Father <term>Kongtse</term> who Subdues Rocks; and the unique Mother, the Single Braid with Crystal Eyes. The unique Father <term>Ava</term> with an Ox Head; and the unique Mother, the Gray-White One with Bared Fangs. The unique Father, the Lord of Death <term>Yavati</term>; and the unique Mother with the fierce gait of a brown bear. The unique Father, the Lord of Death with Red Eyes; and the unique Mother with Blood-Red Braids. The unique Father with Blood-Red Braids; and the unique Mother, the Singer who walks on her knees. The unique Father, the Lord of Death <term>Telpa</term>; and the unique Mother, the Three-Eyed Wind Goddess. The unique Father, the Lord of Death who Subdues Demons; and the unique Mother, the Dark Maroon...
<leaf-break/>

## The Sutra of the Lotus-Colored One

The setting was in Shravasti. At that time, the Venerable Nyede <note>likely Upananda</note> was traveling through the countryside to guard the regions and came to a mountain hermitage. The setting was in Shravasti. At that time, the Venerable Upasena was traveling through the countryside to provide protection and arrived at a mountain retreat. <translation page="64">
Focusing on the Buddha for the sake of omniscience itself, and training in the method of selflessness, is the training in following the Lord of Dharma of the Buddhas; it is training in the knowledge of the path of the Bodhisattva.
Therefore, the state of no-more-learning <note>original: "mi slob pa"; the stage of an Arhat or Buddha where further training is unnecessary</note> is grasped through the power of wisdom and skill-in-means; thus it is no-more-learning in a sequential manner. For that very reason, realizing the unmistakable is the meaning of "training."
By fully knowing the stages of definitive penetration as taught, one will fully know the path of the Pratyekabuddhas <gloss>Solitary Realizers</gloss>. To show that definitive penetration, the phrase "increase of form" and so forth was spoken. Regarding that, by describing the general nature, "form" here refers to the five aggregates of clinging. "Increase" means accumulation. "Decline" means the absence of accumulation. "Grasping" means to rely upon, and so forth.
The one who fully knows the determination to meditate on the aspects as taught is a learner; one who is entering the path. One whose mind is enlightened is a non-learner. Regarding the aggregates of clinging which are to be abandoned, one does not train in grasping the increase or decline of the aggregates. One does not train for the sake of grasping the increase or decrease of the various things to be adopted, such as the applications of mindfulness.
For that very reason, the Buddha does not grasp omniscience itself; it is not even shown by the mind, because that would be a bond. Having emerged in such a way, this is the training:

<leaf-break/>

Having the nature of compassion that is without an object of focus is to delight in Buddhahood itself. By this, the meaning of the term "being" <term>sattva</term> is shown. By that, it is shown that for a Bodhisattva, after abandoning the presentation of reflected images associated with "great being" <term>mahāsattva</term>, it is the Perfection of Wisdom itself that is to be heard. It is not that those forms alone are the definitive case; rather, because the three types of enlightenment cannot occur without it, it is shown as being under its influence.
Although it is spoken of with the general term "Perfection of Wisdom," nevertheless, by the power of convention and so forth, it is understood as a specific meaning. This is because the Perfection of Wisdom is the nature of the mind of enlightenment <term>bodhicitta</term> which encompasses the aspects of all phenomena.
Thus it is said: by thoroughly awakening the seed of great compassion, and by taking the Bodhisattva vows and so forth, one generates the mind of enlightenment characterized by emptiness and compassion as its core. Having attained perfectly complete Buddhahood, one makes the prayer: "I shall act for the benefit of others according to their fortune." Then, to bring that accomplishment to perfection, one aspires to the realization of perfectly complete enlightenment, which is defined by the desire to focus on the benefit of others along with its causes. By generating the mind that has the nature of engagement through the stages of the levels such as the "collections," one reaches up to the Buddha level "Thorough Light" <note>the eleventh level of a Bodhisattva</note> where all aspects are...

<leaf-break/>

The word "also" is used for the purpose of emphasis. Any Bodhisattva who thus fully knows all phenomena, such as the internal self and so forth, through the aspect of the reality that is without signs, does not touch Nirvana. This is because they possess the power of skill-in-means regarding the conventional. "Not touching" means not perceiving as a findable object.

If you ask "What are its aspects?", the text says "this wisdom is..." and so forth. Among these things like form and so forth, which one is it? Is it a substance, a quality, an action, a generality, a particularity, or an inherence? Who is it—is it the self, or is it related to form and so forth? From what does it arise—is it from a self or a phenomenon? Or is it in a self or in a phenomenon? Because all these phenomena are not born in reality.

However, these things like form are empty, similar to the element of space. Because they are not born through reasoning, all phenomena lack the characteristic of being different as support and supported. Up until the statement that they do not exist as various distinct natures. Thus it is said: parts...

...to that as well, because of being harmed by valid cognition, it is coursing in signs.

Because it is the support for the path of seeing and so forth, it is the Abode; coursing in it without attachment or clinging is the practice.
Therefore, in that which has utterly abandoned intrinsic nature, perceiving form and so forth as qualified by the lack of intrinsic nature and so on is the practice; it is shown to be the object of focus.

Because the apprehended is non-existent, the Bodhisattva who courses without perceiving the "grasper" is again "coursing"—this is not perceiving, meaning not realizing.
Because of being utterly unshakable in all aspects by focusing on the aspects of wisdom such as form being without intrinsic nature, it is called the "teaching of wisdom." By that, the transformed state is shown.

<leaf-break/>

...it is, because it is the cause for gradual attainment. Up to the phrase "it is the application <term>prayoga</term>, the practice."
In order for these four types of conceptualization to be understood by the people to be tamed who are gathered in the circle, the Blessed One previously spoke of nine aspects for each one, having divided them by the distinctions of objects. To possess that is to be "together with." By that, having generated the knowledge of hearing and so forth, "possessing discernment" means reasoning...
</translation>

<translation page="64">
For the sake of omniscience itself, having focused upon the Buddha, the training in the method of habituating oneself to selflessness is the training of a follower of the Buddha, the Lord of Dharma; it is the training in the knowledge of the path of a Bodhisattva.
Therefore, the "one beyond training" <note>Sanskrit: aśaikṣa</note> is one who has been fully embraced by the power of wisdom and skill-in-means, and thus, in sequential order, does not train. For that very reason, realizing the non-erroneous is what is meant by "the meaning of training."
That thorough knowledge of the "levels leading to penetration" <note>Sanskrit: nirvedhabhāgīya; the four preliminary stages of the path of connection</note>, as previously explained, will become the thorough knowledge of the path of the Pratyekabuddhas. In order to demonstrate these levels leading to penetration, the passage beginning with "the increase of form" was spoken. In that context, regarding the description of general natures, "form" here refers to the five aggregates of clinging. "Increase" is accumulation. "Degeneration" is the absence of accumulation. "Fully grasping" refers to the process of relying on them.
The thorough knowledge that determines the meditation on the aspects as they were explained belongs to the "one who is training" <note>Sanskrit: śaikṣa</note>; it is that which causes one to enter. That in which the Mind of Enlightenment <note>Sanskrit: bodhicitta</note> is found is the state of "non-training." Regarding the aggregates of clinging which are to be abandoned, one does not train in the full grasping of the increase or degeneration of the aggregates. Regarding the various phenomena to be adopted, such as the applications of mindfulness and so forth, one does not train for the purpose of fully grasping their increase or decrease.
For that very reason, the Buddha does not fully grasp omniscience itself, nor does he demonstrate it through the mind, because it would be a bond. Emerging through such means, one trains in this:

<leaf-break/>

Having the nature of compassion that is without a focal object, one delights in Buddhahood itself. By this, the meaning of the term "Being" <note>referring to the 'sattva' in Bodhisattva</note> is shown. By that, it is demonstrated that after one has abandoned the presentation of the reflected image connected to a "Great Being," and understands that the Perfection of Wisdom itself is what must be heard, it does not mean "only those forms." This is because the three types of Enlightenment <note>the enlightenment of Hearers, Solitary Realizers, and perfect Buddhas</note> do not occur if that is absent, and thus they are shown as being under its influence. Although it is spoken of using the general term "Perfection of Wisdom," nevertheless, by the power of convention and so forth, it is understood to be a specific meaning. This is because the Perfection of Wisdom is the nature of the Mind of Enlightenment that summarizes the aspects of all phenomena. Thus, it is said: by thoroughly awakening the seed of Great Compassion, one takes the Bodhisattva vows and so forth, and generates the Mind of Enlightenment characterized by emptiness and the essence of compassion. After attaining perfectly complete Buddhahood, one makes the prayer: "I shall act for the benefit of others according to their fortune," and thus brings the accomplishment to perfection. This refers to the aspiration, which is the characteristic of the desire to realize perfectly complete Enlightenment—the fruit together with its cause—focusing on the welfare of others. It also refers to the generation of the mind of engagement, which progresses through the stages such as the "Paths of Accumulation" up to the Buddha stage of "Universal Radiance" <note>Sanskrit: Samantaprabhā; the eleventh bhūmi or stage</note>, where every aspect...

<leaf-break/>

The word "also" <note>Tibetan: 'ang</note> carries the sense of certain grasping. Any Bodhisattva who, in that way, through the aspect of the reality of the thorough knowledge that all phenomena—such as the internal self and so forth—are without signs, does not touch Nirvana because they possess the power of skill-in-means regarding the conventional. "Not touching" means "not apprehending." By the power of the ultimate truth, they abide in the Perfection of Wisdom; they abide in the expanse of phenomena <term>dharmadhātu</term>. This refers to the apprehension of form and so forth, which are distinguished by being without signs and so on; it includes the result. If you ask "What are its aspects?", the passage beginning with "This wisdom..." is spoken. Among these things like form and so forth, what is it? Is it a substance, or a quality, or an action, or a universal, or a particular, or an inherence? Who is it? Is it a "self," or is it something connected to form and so forth? From what does it arise? Is it from a self or a phenomenon? Or is it in a self or a phenomenon? Furthermore, is it from a self or from a phenomenon? This is because all these phenomena are not produced in reality. The word "what" should be applied to all: this is not "anything," it belongs to "no one," and it is "in nothing." This is the investigative meditation of wisdom that does not apprehend any phenomena. "Close examination" means investigating those things closely. "Analytical movement" means the Bodhisattva enters by subsequently apprehending these aspects.
</translation>

If that is so, why does the "One Hundred Thousand Verse Sutra" <note>the Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</note> show the knowledge of the Bodhisattva path and so forth as distinct? It is said: because omniscience, looking toward the attainment of the fruit together with its cause, is the Blessed Buddha...

<leaf-break/>

It will be shown as being an "aspect." If you ask for what purpose it is the cause, the passage "having closely examined" is spoken. Its focal object and aspects are the various aspects just demonstrated. Having closely examined all phenomena as being emptiness, because there is no attachment, there is no discouragement. Because it is endowed with reasoning, there is no fear. Furthermore, the entry into reality without error is the "Peak" <note>Sanskrit: murdhā; the second stage of the path of connection</note>. Through realizing the divisions of small, medium, and great, the hearing of any enlightenment such as that of the Hearers becomes the cause for all enlightenment and for the Bodhisattva's proximity [to it].
Following the "Peak" is "Patience" <note>Sanskrit: kṣānti; the third stage of the path of connection</note>. Because of the great patience for phenomena characterized by the absence of the lower realms, the passage beginning with "If..." is spoken to show the focal object of that which has become patience. "If one practices without knowledge" means practicing without realizing selflessness. "Investigation" is conceptualization. "Practicing with signs" is practicing the opposite. It means that while not knowing reality, one practices with an obsession for form—from the general characteristic of form up to consciousness. This is because such [obsession] is invalidated by valid cognition, like the perception of a mirage. It is connected to the phrase "He practices with the signs of a focal object." That is what is shown. Similarly, if one investigates and becomes obsessed, thinking "the five aggregates like form are empty," if one practices without realizing the nature of phenomena, then at that time, because even that obsession with "emptiness" is invalidated by valid cognition...
</translation>

<translation page="66">
...even in that, because it is invalidated by valid cognition, it is a "practice with signs." Similarly, the Bodhisattva who practices by reversing the obsession with the nature of things and non-things is one who practices by abiding in the state of non-arising. Because it is the support for the Path of Seeing and so forth, "abiding" means that practicing without attachment or obsession is the true practice. Therefore, in the total abandonment of nature, focusing on form and so forth as distinguished by "lack of nature" and so on is the practice; it is shown as being the focal object.
If you ask "What kind of aspect is that?", the passage beginning with "Whatever form..." is spoken. By whatever means one practices without abiding due to non-arising, from the absence of form up to consciousness, one does not practice with obsession for them as "objects to be grasped" and does not experience them.
Because there is no "object to be grasped," the Bodhisattva who practices without apprehending a "grasper" is again one whose "practice" is not apprehended; it is not realized. Because of the focus on the aspects of the nature of wisdom—the lack of inherent nature in form and so forth—it is called the "teaching of wisdom" because it is completely unshakable by any aspects or signs. By that, the transformation is shown.
If you ask for what purpose it is the cause, the passage beginning with "The wise one of non-arising..." is spoken. Similarly, that wise one who realizes the focal objects and aspects as being without arising, having understood the divisions of small, medium, and great patience, possesses the nature of a one-pointed mind...

<leaf-break/>

A "child" <note>Sanskrit: bāla; an ordinary person</note> is one in whom the path of the Noble Ones has not arisen. Its "sign" <note>referring to 'linga' or mark</note> is to be understood through reasoning. These phenomena, just as they appear, exist. According to reasoning, they do not exist. Furthermore, that which is to be abandoned is based on the totally afflicted. The very object of the first conceptualization of the "grasped" is ignorance; it acts in accordance with total affliction. "Acting" means "positing," just as one posits that which is to be purified.
Similarly, that which is to be adopted is based on the remedy. The very object of the second conceptualization of the "grasped" is the "reason"; it is posited in accordance with [correct] conceptualization. Having thus established the conceptualization of the grasped, from this point forward, the demonstration of how those two, together with the objects of obsession, are to be meditated upon as being false like an illusion, is given in the passage beginning with "Knowledge and ignorance." These two, knowledge and ignorance, are phenomena that do not exist as form and so forth, because they are not produced in reality. It is the "child" who, by the power of manifest pride, conceptualizes them as "knowledge" and "ignorance."
The Bodhisattva who, through the stages of hearing and so forth, understands them thoroughly, emerges; he emerges by truly entering [the path] from the bonds of error. To show the first conceptualization of the "grasper" <note>the subject</note> that follows the two conceptualizations of the "grasped" <note>the object</note>, the passage beginning with "Which..." is spoken. Any Bodhisattva who, by the power of reasoning, [views] the aggregates as a deceptive illusion, [overcomes] the conceptualization that grasps the five aggregates as having the nature of a substantially existent person...

<leaf-break/>

...it is, because it is the cause for gradual attainment. It continues until the phrase "it is the practice <term>yoga</term> that causes one to experience."
In order for these four types of conceptualization to be understood by the people to be tamed who are gathered in the circle, the Blessed One previously spoke in detail, dividing them by the distinctions of objects, and spoke of nine aspects for each. However, here, the essentials are summarized and shown. There is no need for an extensive demonstration, and the Blessed One, considering that the divisions of objects in the "One Hundred Thousand Verse Sutra" were not the primary focus here, made this [summary] from the perspective of the "levels leading to penetration." The division of the base by objects is one thing, and the demonstration of the divisions of conceptualization from the perspective of the realization of the "Peak" and the Path of Meditation is another.
Since this is the essence, from that characteristic which exists by excluding [the opposite], there are no other aggregates. One should understand the subsequent ones in the same way, following the two types of conceptualization—the conceptualization of the "grasped" and the conceptualization of the "grasper"—as they have been explained.
This shows the "full grasping" which has the nature of the Spiritual Friend and skill-in-means. Because of their power, the previously mentioned distinctions occur. Thus, the passage beginning with "Virtue..." is spoken. Because he is a person who demonstrates the Dharma without departing from the two truths and causes one to obtain the fruit of a happy rebirth, he is a "Spiritual Friend" <note>Sanskrit: kalyāṇamitra</note>. To "possess" that is to be "with" him. By generating the knowledge of hearing and so forth through that very [friend], the "one with discernment" is the "reason"...
</translation>

<summary>
This page details the stages of the Bodhisattva path, specifically focusing on the four levels leading to penetration (heat, peak, patience, and supreme dharma) and the abandonment of conceptual grasping. It emphasizes that ultimate wisdom involves realizing the non-arising and illusory nature of all phenomena, including the path itself and the concept of a self.
</summary>

Is it from a self or a phenomenon? Or is it in a self or a phenomenon? Furthermore, is it from a self or from a phenomenon? This is because all these phenomena are not produced in reality. By fully knowing those facets of the "stages of penetration," one will fully know the path of the Pratyekabuddhas as it was taught. To demonstrate the stages of penetration, it is said, "form increases" and so forth. Regarding that, by expressing the general nature: "form" here refers to the five aggregates of grasping. "Increasing" means accumulating. "Degeneration" means the absence of accumulation. "Fully grasping" means to rely upon, and so forth.

That which is the mind of awakening <term>bodhicitta</term> is "no-more-learning." Regarding the aggregates of grasping which are to be abandoned, one does not train in fully grasping the increase or degeneration of the aggregates. One does not train for the sake of fully grasping the increase or decrease of the various phenomena to be adopted, such as the applications of mindfulness.

...because that too is invalidated by valid cognition, it is "practicing with signs." Likewise, after being obsessed with the nature of things as existent and non-existent, the Mind of Awakening <term>bodhicitta</term> which practices in reverse of that is the very state of non-production. Because it is the support for the path of seeing and so forth, it "abides"; and to practice without attachment or obsession for that is the "practice." Therefore, to focus on form and so forth characterized by the absence of nature while having entirely abandoned nature—that is the "practice"; it is shown to be the focal point. If one asks "Which aspect is that?", it is said: "That which is form..." and so forth. That which is practicing without abiding because of non-production; not practicing with obsession for "taking up" and not experiencing the absence of things from form down to consciousness. That Bodhisattva who practices without perceiving the "grasper" because there is no "grasped," is again "practicing"—thus it is not perceived, meaning not realized. Because of being utterly unshakable by all aspects of the signs through focusing on the aspects of the nature of wisdom such as the non-existence of form and so forth, it is called the "demonstration of wisdom." By that, the "transformation" is shown. If one asks "What is the cause for this purpose?", it is said: "The wise one without production..." and so forth. Likewise, that wise one who realizes the focal points and aspects as unproduced, having realized the distinctions of small, medium, and great patience, has the nature of a one-pointed mind...

<leaf-break/>

A "child" is one in whom the Noble Path has not arisen. Its "mark" is being endowed with reasoning. These phenomena, just as they appear, exist. According to reasoning, they do not exist just as they appear. Again, that which is to be abandoned is the basis for thorough affliction. In the first domain of the conceptualization of the "grasped" is ignorance; it acts in accordance with thorough affliction. Because "acting" means "depositing," it is like depositing that which is to be purified. Likewise, in the second domain of the conceptualization of the "grasped" which is the basis for the antidote to be adopted, it is reasoning; it is deposited in accordance with non-conceptualization. Having thus established the conceptualization of the "grasped," and having started from these two right here, the demonstration of the meditation on them as false and illusion-like together with the objects of obsession is said: "knowledge and ignorance" and so forth. These two, knowledge and ignorance, because they are unproduced in reality, are phenomena that do not exist in form and so forth; it is by the power of manifest pride that the "child" conceptualizes "knowledge" and "ignorance." Any Bodhisattva who thoroughly knows through the sequence of hearing and so forth "emerges"; he emerges by having perfectly entered into the state of freedom from the bonds of error. Following the two conceptualizations of the "grasped," in order to show the first conceptualization of the "grasper," it is said, "Who..." and so forth. Any Bodhisattva who, through the power of reasoning, sees the five aggregates—which are the conceptualization of grasping the person as a substantially existent nature—as the illusion and error of the aggregates...

<leaf-break/>

...it is so; because it is the cause for gradual attainment. Up to the phrase "it is the application, the engagement in experience." In order for these four conceptualizations to be understood by the people to be tamed who are gathered in the circle, previously the Blessed One spoke of nine aspects for each by dividing them according to the categories of objects; however, here the principal points are shown in summary. There is no need for an extensive presentation, and the Blessed One, considering that the divisions of objects in the *One Hundred Thousand Stanza Sutra* are not the primary concern here, made the division of objects as the ground while presiding over the facets of the "stages of penetration." Furthermore, the presentation of the divisions of conceptualization made in view of the seeing of the "Peak Realization" and the path of meditation is also different. Because this is the "Essence," from that characteristic of abiding while mutually abandoning, there are no other aggregates; therefore, one should realize that the subsequent ones follow in the same way as the two conceptualizations of the "grasped" and the "grasper" which were taught. This shows the "full grasping" which has the nature of the spiritual friend and skill in means. Because by that power, what was taught becomes specific, it is said "virtuous" and so forth. Because the person who teaches the Dharma without departing from the two truths causes the attainment of the result of a happy migration, they are a "spiritual friend" <term>kalyāṇamitra</term>. To be "endowed with that" means to be together with them. Having generated the knowledge of hearing and so forth through that very [friend], "endowed with discernment" means reasoning...
</translation>

<summary>
This text provides a commentary on the stages of the Bodhisattva path, specifically focusing on the Perfection of Wisdom, the stages of penetration, and the four types of conceptualization regarding the grasped and the grasper. It emphasizes that realization involves seeing all phenomena, from form to omniscience, as unproduced, empty, and illusion-like, while maintaining skill in means and compassion.
</summary>

For the sake of omniscience itself, having focused upon the Buddha, the training in the method of habituating oneself to selflessness is the training in the Buddha's Lordship of Dharma; it is training in the knowledge of the Bodhisattva's path.
Therefore, the state of "no-more-learning" is being fully embraced by the power of wisdom and skill in means; thus, in successive order, there is no more learning. For that very reason, the realization of the non-erroneous is what is meant by the term "training."
By fully knowing those facets of the "stages of penetration," one will fully know the path of the Pratyekabuddhas as it was taught. To demonstrate the stages of penetration, it is said, "form increases" and so forth. Regarding that, by expressing the general nature: "form" here refers to the five aggregates of grasping. "Increasing" means accumulating. "Degeneration" means the absence of accumulation. "Fully grasping" means to rely upon, and so forth.
The full knowledge that determines the meditation on the aspects as they were taught is the stage of "learning"; it is that which causes one to enter. That which is the mind of awakening <term>bodhicitta</term> is "no-more-learning." Regarding the aggregates of grasping which are to be abandoned, one does not train in fully grasping the increase or degeneration of the aggregates. One does not train for the sake of fully grasping the increase or decrease of the various phenomena to be adopted, such as the applications of mindfulness.
For that very reason, the Buddha does not fully grasp omniscience itself; he does not even indicate it with the mind. This is because it would be a bond. Having emerged in such a way, one trains in this:

<leaf-break/>

Having the nature of compassion without focal points, one delights in Buddhahood itself. This shows the meaning of the term "Being" <term>sattva</term> in "Awakening Being" <term>bodhisattva</term>. By that, it is shown that here, after having abandoned the presentation of the reflected image associated with the Great Being <term>mahāsattva</term>, that which is to be heard is the Perfection of Wisdom <term>prajñāpāramitā</term> itself; it is not that those forms alone are meant. This is because if the three kinds of awakening do not exist, they do not arise; therefore, it will be shown for the sake of taking mastery. Although it is spoken in the general term "Perfection of Wisdom," nevertheless, by the power of convention and so forth, it is understood as a specific meaning. This is because the Perfection of Wisdom is the nature of the mind of awakening which summarizes the aspects of all phenomena. Thus, it is said: by thoroughly awakening the seed of great compassion, one adopts the Bodhisattva vows and so forth, and generates the mind of awakening which has the essence of emptiness and compassion. After having made the prayer, "Having attained perfectly complete Buddhahood, I shall act for the sake of others according to their fortune," one shall bring the practice to perfection. The aspiration, which is the characteristic of the desire to realize perfectly complete awakening—the fruit together with the cause focused on the benefit of others—and the generation of the mind of the nature of engagement, through the sequence of the stages such as the path of accumulation, up to the Buddha's "Universal Radiance" <term>samantaprabhā</term>, which is all aspects...

<leaf-break/>

The word "also" has the meaning of emphasis. Any Bodhisattva who, in that way, has the aspect of the reality of fully knowing all phenomena—such as the internal self—as being signless: they do not touch nirvana because they possess the power of skill in means regarding the conventional. "Not touching" means not perceiving as a focal point. By the power of the ultimate, they abide in the Perfection of Wisdom; they abide in the expanse of phenomena <term>dharmadhātu</term>. This is the perception of specific forms and so forth through signlessness and so forth; it is possessed of the result. If one asks "What is its aspect?", it is said: "This wisdom..." and so forth. Among these things such as form, which one is it? Is it a substance? A quality? An action? A universal? A particular? An inherence? Who is it—is it a "self"? Is it related to form and so forth? From what does it come—from a self? From a phenomenon? In what does it exist? Or does it come from a self or from a phenomenon? This is because all these phenomena are, in reality, unproduced. The word "what" should be applied everywhere: this is not anything, it belongs to no one, it exists in nothing. This is the thorough investigation by wisdom without perceiving any phenomena. "Close examination" is the close investigation of those. "Engaging" is when the Bodhisattva enters after having subsequently perceived these aspects.

Because of delighting in habituation, the Blessed One is omniscience itself. The phrase "gradually" is the remainder of the sentence. Regarding the abandonment of the remaining afflictions: because one is oriented toward the essence of the path shown previously, the repeated focusing is what is established as the path of meditation. By the very fact of fully knowing the path of seeing, that is established as being fully known; therefore, so that Bodhisattvas may fully know it, it should be understood that it is not spoken of as a distinct part of meditation associated with the Hearers and so forth, just like the path of seeing. By the power of the seeing and so forth of the Son of the Conqueror who has become such, having attained mastery over his own path, he wins over sentient beings who are to be tamed by other vehicles; therefore, he is completely victorious over both paths.
Likewise, there is no wisdom in form; this is for the sake of realizing the path of seeing which possesses the great benefits associated with consciousness and so forth. Form is not wisdom; it does not exist in suchness.
Likewise, there is no wisdom apart from form; there is no wisdom in any of the factors such as consciousness; it is the same for wisdom itself. However, similar to the element of space, these things such as form are empty. Because they are not produced by reasoning, all phenomena lack the characteristic of being distinct as support and supported; they do not exist as various specific natures—up to this point it is taught. Thus it is said: parts...

<leaf-break/>

...the nature of those things which are to be realized. It will be shown by the meaning: "One should generate and accomplish the knowledge of hearing and so forth of the illusion-like Perfection of Wisdom." If one asks: "If the Sons of the Conquerors have accomplished the knowledge of the path and so forth, how does that generation of the mind, which is the essence of omniscience itself, relate to those?", it is said, "wherein the Heroes practice." "Wherein" refers to the Perfection of Wisdom. Those who are victorious over all phenomena of the discordant side and who cannot be diminished are the "Heroes." The Bodhisattvas, by possessing habituation to the entirety of the "practice of the Heroes," enter into that which is the very essence of the production <note>of the mind</note>; this is the meaning of "it is the Perfection of Wisdom." Therefore, the mind shown in this way has no other phenomenon separate from the Dharma; even the instructions and so forth are only the distinctions of the generation of the mind for the sake of showing the specific meaning. Therefore, that nature which is omniscience itself will be shown first, having summarized all the phenomena to be attained by the Bodhisattva. It will be shown that "it is shown first." If that is so, why is it that in the *One Hundred Thousand Stanza Sutra* the knowledge of the path of the Bodhisattva and so forth are shown as distinct? It is said: because omniscience itself is the result together with its cause, in view of its attainment, the Buddha, the Blessed One...

<leaf-break/>

...it will be shown to be an aspect. If you ask "What is the cause for this purpose?", it is said: "having closely examined." Having closely examined all phenomena as emptiness through the various aspects of its focal points and the aspects just described, because there is no attachment, there is no discouragement. Because it is endowed with reasoning, there is no fear. Furthermore, the "Peak" is the entry into reality without error; by realizing the distinctions of small, medium, and great, the hearing of any awakening such as that of the Hearers is shown to be the cause of all awakenings and the Bodhisattva's proximity <note>to awakening</note>.
Following the Peak, there is now "Patience"; because of the great Dharma of patience characterized by the absence of miserable rebirths, for the sake of showing the focal point of the state of patience, it is said, "If..." and so forth. "If one practices without knowledge" means practicing without having realized selflessness. "Thorough investigation" means conceptualization. "Practicing with signs" means practicing the opposite. This is stated: if, without knowing the reality of things, one is obsessed with form through the general characteristics of form, down to consciousness, then that is like the cognition of a mirage and so forth, because it is invalidated by valid cognition. "Practicing with the signs of a focal point"—it is connected to this. So it will be shown. Likewise, if one thoroughly investigates and becomes obsessed, thinking "these five aggregates such as form are empty," and if one practices without realizing the nature of phenomena, then at that time, being obsessed with emptiness...

<translation page="64">
Seeking omniscience itself for the sake of the Buddha, and then familiarizing oneself with the method of selflessness, is the training in the Lord of Dharma, the Buddha; it is training in the knowledge of the path of the Bodhisattva.
Therefore, the state of non-training is being fully embraced by the power of wisdom and skill in methods; thus, one sequentially does not train. For that very reason, it is said that realizing the non-erroneous is the training. Having fully understood the portion of definite differentiation, as previously explained, one will fully understand the path of the Pratyekabuddhas. To show that definite differentiation, the passage beginning with "increase of form" was spoken. In that context, speaking of the general nature, "form" here refers to the five aggregates of clinging. "Increase" is accumulation. "Degeneration" is the absence of accumulation. "Full grasping" refers to making a transition, and so on.
The full understanding that determines the meditation on the aspects as they have been explained is the path of training; it is that which causes entry. That in which the mind of enlightenment does not train is non-training. Regarding the aggregates of clinging which are to be abandoned, one does not train in order to fully grasp the increase or degeneration of the aggregates. One does not train for the sake of fully grasping the increase or decrease of the various phenomena to be adopted, such as the applications of mindfulness.
For that very reason, the Buddha does not fully grasp omniscience itself, and it is not even shown by the mind, because that would be a bond. Having emerged in such a way, one trains in this:
<leaf-break/>
In the nature of compassion without an object, one rejoices in Buddhahood itself. By this, the meaning of the word "Being" <note>Sanskrit: Sattva</note> is shown. By that, it is shown that after discarding the presentation of a reflection connected to a Bodhisattva Mahasattva, the perfection of wisdom itself is what should be heard; it is not that those forms alone are meant. Because if those three types of enlightenment were absent, it would not occur, it is shown for the sake of mastery. Although it is spoken in the general term "Perfection of Wisdom," nevertheless, by the power of convention and so forth, it is understood to be the specific meaning, because the perfection of wisdom is the nature of the mind of enlightenment that summarizes the aspects of all phenomena. By that, it says: because the seed of great compassion is fully awakened, one takes the Bodhisattva vows and so forth, and generates the mind of enlightenment characterized by emptiness and the essence of compassion. After attaining perfectly complete Buddhahood, one makes the prayer: "I shall act for the benefit of others according to their fortune," and thus brings the practice to perfection. The prayer, which is the defining characteristic of the desire to realize perfectly complete enlightenment—the fruit together with its cause—objectifying the benefit of others, and the generation of the mind that has the nature of engagement, proceed through the stages of the grounds such as the "Collections" up to the Buddha ground "Universal Radiance" <note>Sanskrit: Samantaprabha</note>, which is all aspects...
<leaf-break/>
The word "also" has the meaning of emphasis. Any Bodhisattva who, in such a way, understands all phenomena such as the internal self to be without signs through the aspect of reality, does not touch nirvana, because they possess the power of skill in conventional methods. "Not touching" means not objectifying. By the power of the ultimate, they abide in the perfection of wisdom, in the sphere of phenomena <note>Sanskrit: Dharmadhatu</note>. This is the objectification of form and so forth, characterized by being signless and so on, which is possessed of a result. What is its aspect? The passage beginning with "this wisdom..." was spoken: among these things such as form, which one is it? Is it a substance, or a quality, or an action, or a generality, or a particularity, or an inherence? Who is it? Is it a self? Is it connected to form and so forth? From what does it come: a self or a phenomenon? Or is it from a self or from a phenomenon? Because all these phenomena are not born in reality. The word "what" should be applied everywhere: it is not anything, it does not belong to anyone, it is not in anything; thus one investigates through wisdom without objectifying any phenomena. "Close examination" is the close investigation of those; "analytical engagement" is the Bodhisattva's entry after subsequently objectifying these aspects.
</translation>
<translation page="65">
Because of rejoicing in familiarity, the Blessed One is omniscience itself; the phrase "gradually" is an additional word. As for the abandonment of the remaining afflictions, because facing the nature of the path previously shown and objectifying it again and again is established as the path of meditation, therefore, by the very fact that the path of seeing is fully understood, it is established as fully understood. Thus, for the sake of the Bodhisattvas' full understanding, one should understand it without describing it as a distinct part of the meditation path connected with Hearers and so forth, as was done for the path of seeing. Through the power of the vision of the Sons of the Conquerors who have become such, having attained mastery over their own path, they are victorious over the two paths because they embrace sentient beings to be tamed by other vehicles.
Likewise, there is no wisdom in form; this is for the sake of realizing the path of seeing which has great benefits and is possessed of consciousness and so forth. Form is not wisdom; it does not exist in suchness. Likewise, there is no wisdom from form; there is no wisdom in any of the categories like consciousness, and the same applies to wisdom itself. However, like the element of space, these things such as form are empty; because they are not born through reasoning, all phenomena lack the characteristic of being distinct as support and supported; they lack a nature of various distinctions—up to that point. As it is said: parts...
<leaf-break/>
The nature of those things to be realized: the perfection of wisdom is like an illusion; one should generate and accomplish the knowledge of hearing and so forth—this is shown by the meaning. If one asks: "Since the Sons of the Conquerors accomplish the knowledge of the path and so forth, how does that generation of the mind, which has the nature of omniscience itself, relate to those?" the passage beginning with "that in which the heroes course" was spoken. "That in which" refers to the perfection of wisdom. "Heroes course" refers to those who are victorious over all phenomena of the discordant side and cannot be degenerated; such ones are the nature of the generation of the mind, which is the perfection of wisdom, because they possess familiarity with all courses—that is the meaning. Therefore, the mind shown in this way has no other phenomena apart from the Dharma; even the instructions and so forth are only divisions of the generation of the mind for the sake of showing the specific meaning. Therefore, its nature, omniscience itself, will be shown first, having summarized all the phenomena to be attained by a Bodhisattva. It will be shown that it is "shown first." If that is so, why does the *Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred Thousand Lines* show the Bodhisattva's knowledge of the path and so forth as distinct? It is said: because omniscience itself is the attainment of the fruit together with its cause, it is in reference to the Buddha, the Blessed One...
<leaf-break/>
...will be shown to be the aspect. If you ask for what purpose it is the cause: the passage "having closely examined" was spoken. Having closely examined all phenomena as emptiness through the various aspects of its object and aspects just explained, there is no discouragement because there is no attachment. Because of being endowed with reasoning, there is no fear. Furthermore, that which enters reality without error is the "Peak," and by realizing the divisions of small, medium, and great, the hearing of any enlightenment such as that of a Hearer is shown to be the proximity of all enlightenment and the Bodhisattva; it is shown to be the cause. After the Peak comes "Patience"; because it is the great Dharma patience characterized by the absence of lower realms, in order to show the object of having become patient, the passage beginning with "If" was spoken. "If one courses without knowing" means coursing without realizing selflessness. "Investigation" is conceptualization. "Coursing in signs" is coursing in the opposite. Thus, not knowing the nature of reality and being attached to form from the general characteristic of form down to consciousness—that is because it is harmed by valid cognition, like the perception of a mirage and so forth. "Coursing in the signs of an object"—thus it is connected. So it will be shown. Likewise, if one investigates the five aggregates such as form as "empty" and is attached to that, and if one courses without realizing the nature of phenomena, then at that time, being attached to "emptiness"...
</translation>
<translation page="66">
...because that is also harmed by valid cognition, it is "coursing in signs." Likewise, after being attached to the nature of existence and non-existence, the Bodhisattva who courses in the opposite of that courses in the state which is the very birthless state; because it is the support for the path of seeing and so forth, it is the state; coursing without clinging to it and without attachment is the practice. Therefore, objectifying form and so forth characterized by the absence of nature while having abandoned nature entirely is the practice; it is shown to be the object. If you ask what its aspect is, the passage beginning with "That which is form..." was spoken. One who courses without a state because of birthlessness: the absence of everything from form to consciousness means one does not course in the attachment of grasping and does not experience it. Because there is no grasped, the Bodhisattva who courses without objectifying the grasper is again said to be "coursing"; thus they do not objectify and do not realize. Because of objectifying the nature of the wisdom of form and so forth as being without nature, one is completely unshakable by all aspects and signs; thus it is called "teaching wisdom." By that, the transformation is shown. If you ask for what purpose it is the cause: the passage beginning with "The wise one without birth" was spoken. Likewise, that wise one who realizes the objects and aspects as birthless, having realized the divisions of small, medium, and great patience, has a nature of one-pointed mental concentration...
<leaf-break/>
A "child" <note>Sanskrit: bala</note> is one in whom the path of the Aryas has not been born. Its "sign" is in accordance with reasoning. These phenomena as they appear are "existent." According to reasoning as it actually is, they are "non-existent." Furthermore, that which is to be abandoned is the basis of affliction. Ignorance itself is the first object of the conceptualization of the grasped; it acts in accordance with affliction. "Acting" means placing, just as one places what is to be purified. Likewise, what is to be adopted is the second object of the conceptualization of the grasped, based on the antidote; it is reasoning, and it is placed in accordance with conceptualization. Having thus established the conceptualization of the grasped, from this point onwards those two, together with the object of attachment, are shown to be meditated upon as false, like an illusion; thus the passage beginning with "knowledge and ignorance" was spoken. These two, knowledge and ignorance, are phenomena that do not exist as form and so forth because they are not born in reality; they are imputed as "knowledge" and "ignorance" by children through the power of manifest pride. Any Bodhisattva who knows this through the sequence of hearing and so forth emerges; by truly entering from the bond of error, they emerge. To show the first conceptualization of the grasper after the two conceptualizations of the grasped, the passage beginning with "Who" was spoken. Any Bodhisattva who, through the power of reasoning, [realizes] the aggregates as a deceptive illusion, [overcomes] the conceptualization of grasping the five aggregates as having a nature of a substantially existent person...
<leaf-break/>
...it is so; because it is the cause of gradual attainment. Up to the phrase "it is the application <note>Sanskrit: prayoga</note>, the engagement in experience." In order for these four conceptualizations to be understood by the people to be tamed who are close to the cycle [of existence], the Blessed One previously explained them in detail by dividing them according to objects, speaking of nine aspects for each. However, here the essentials are summarized and shown; there is no need for a detailed explanation, and the Blessed One, considering that the division by objects in the *One Hundred Thousand Lines* was not the primary focus here, made the division of the bases of the objects in terms of the portions of definite differentiation. The division of the conceptualizations made in terms of the vision of the peak realization and the path of meditation is another matter. Because this is the essence, from that characteristic which exists by mutually excluding [other things], there are no other aggregates; one should understand the subsequent ones in the same way, following the two previously explained conceptualizations of the grasped and the conceptualizations of the grasper. That shows the embracing by the nature of the spiritual friend <note>Sanskrit: kalyanamitra</note> and skill in methods. Because the previous explanation becomes specific through that power, the passage beginning with "Virtuous" was spoken. Because they are a person who teaches the Dharma without departing from the two truths and causes the attainment of the result of a happy migration, they are a "spiritual friend." To be endowed with that is "together with." After generating the knowledge of hearing and so forth through that very thing, "the one with discernment" is reasoning...
</translation>

<summary>This text discusses the stages of Buddhist path realization, specifically focusing on the Bodhisattva's training in the Perfection of Wisdom. it details the conceptualizations of the "grasped" and "grasper" and how to overcome them through the realization of emptiness and birthlessness.</summary>
<keywords>Bodhisattva, Perfection of Wisdom, Emptiness, Path of Seeing, Path of Meditation, Conceptualization, Omniscience, Spiritual Friend, Skill in Methods</keywords>

pages.64:
Seeking omniscience itself for the sake of the Buddha, and then familiarizing oneself with the method of selflessness, is the training in the Lord of Dharma, the Buddha; it is training in the knowledge of the path of the Bodhisattva.
Therefore, the state of non-training is being fully embraced by the power of wisdom and skill in methods; thus, one sequentially does not train. For that very reason, it is said that realizing the non-erroneous is the training. Having fully understood the portion of definite differentiation, as previously explained, one will fully understand the path of the Pratyekabuddhas. To show that definite differentiation, the passage beginning with "increase of form" was spoken. In that context, speaking of the general nature, "form" here refers to the five aggregates of clinging. "Increase" is accumulation. "Degeneration" is the absence of accumulation. "Full grasping" refers to making a transition, and so on.
The full understanding that determines the meditation on the aspects as they have been explained is the path of training; it is that which causes entry. That in which the mind of enlightenment does not train is non-training. Regarding the aggregates of clinging which are to be abandoned, one does not train in order to fully grasp the increase or degeneration of the aggregates. One does not train for the sake of fully grasping the increase or decrease of the various phenomena to be adopted, such as the applications of mindfulness.
For that very reason, the Buddha does not fully grasp omniscience itself, and it is not even shown by the mind, because that would be a bond. Having emerged in such a way, one trains in this:
<leaf-break/>
In the nature of compassion without an object, one rejoices in Buddhahood itself. By this, the meaning of the word "Being" <note>Sanskrit: Sattva</note> is shown. By that, it is shown that after discarding the presentation of a reflection connected to a Bodhisattva Mahasattva, the perfection of wisdom itself is what should be heard; it is not that those forms alone are meant. Because if those three types of enlightenment were absent, it would not occur, it is shown for the sake of mastery. Although it is spoken in the general term "Perfection of Wisdom," nevertheless, by the power of convention and so forth, it is understood to be the specific meaning, because the perfection of wisdom is the nature of the mind of enlightenment that summarizes the aspects of all phenomena. By that, it says: because the seed of great compassion is fully awakened, one takes the Bodhisattva vows and so forth, and generates the mind of enlightenment characterized by emptiness and the essence of compassion. After attaining perfectly complete Buddhahood, one makes the prayer: "I shall act for the benefit of others according to their fortune," and thus brings the practice to perfection. The prayer, which is the defining characteristic of the desire to realize perfectly complete enlightenment—the fruit together with its cause—objectifying the benefit of others, and the generation of the mind that has the nature of engagement, proceed through the stages of the grounds such as the "Collections" up to the Buddha ground "Universal Radiance" <note>Sanskrit: Samantaprabha</note>, which is all aspects...
<leaf-break/>
The word "also" has the meaning of emphasis. Any Bodhisattva who, in such a way, understands all phenomena such as the internal self to be without signs through the aspect of reality, does not touch nirvana, because they possess the power of skill in conventional methods. "Not touching" means not objectifying. By the power of the ultimate, they abide in the perfection of wisdom, in the sphere of phenomena <note>Sanskrit: Dharmadhatu</note>. This is the objectification of form and so forth, characterized by being signless and so on, which is possessed of a result. What is its aspect? The passage beginning with "this wisdom..." was spoken: among these things such as form, which one is it? Is it a substance, or a quality, or an action, or a generality, or a particularity, or an inherence? Who is it? Is it a self? Is it connected to form and so forth? From what does it come: a self or a phenomenon? Or is it from a self or from a phenomenon? Because all these phenomena are not born in reality. The word "what" should be applied everywhere: it is not anything, it does not belong to anyone, it is not in anything; thus one investigates through wisdom without objectifying any phenomena. "Close examination" is the close investigation of those; "analytical engagement" is the Bodhisattva's entry after subsequently objectifying these aspects.
pages.65:
Because of rejoicing in familiarity, the Blessed One is omniscience itself; the phrase "gradually" is an additional word. As for the abandonment of the remaining afflictions, because facing the nature of the path previously shown and objectifying it again and again is established as the path of meditation, therefore, by the very fact that the path of seeing is fully understood, it is established as fully understood. Thus, for the sake of the Bodhisattvas' full understanding, one should understand it without describing it as a distinct part of the meditation path connected with Hearers and so forth, as was done for the path of seeing. Through the power of the vision of the Sons of the Conquerors who have become such, having attained mastery over their own path, they are victorious over the two paths because they embrace sentient beings to be tamed by other vehicles.
Likewise, there is no wisdom in form; this is for the sake of realizing the path of seeing which has great benefits and is possessed of consciousness and so forth. Form is not wisdom; it does not exist in suchness. Likewise, there is no wisdom from form; there is no wisdom in any of the categories like consciousness, and the same applies to wisdom itself. However, like the element of space, these things such as form are empty; because they are not born through reasoning, all phenomena lack the characteristic of being distinct as support and supported; they lack a nature of various distinctions—up to that point. As it is said: parts...
<leaf-break/>
The nature of those things to be realized: the perfection of wisdom is like an illusion; one should generate and accomplish the knowledge of hearing and so forth—this is shown by the meaning. If one asks: "Since the Sons of the Conquerors accomplish the knowledge of the path and so forth, how does that generation of the mind, which has the nature of omniscience itself, relate to those?" the passage beginning with "that in which the heroes course" was spoken. "That in which" refers to the perfection of wisdom. "Heroes course" refers to those who are victorious over all phenomena of the discordant side and cannot be degenerated; such ones are the nature of the generation of the mind, which is the perfection of wisdom, because they possess familiarity with all courses—that is the meaning. Therefore, the mind shown in this way has no other phenomena apart from the Dharma; even the instructions and so forth are only divisions of the generation of the mind for the sake of showing the specific meaning. Therefore, its nature, omniscience itself, will be shown first, having summarized all the phenomena to be attained by a Bodhisattva. It will be shown that it is "shown first." If that is so, why does the *Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred Thousand Lines* show the Bodhisattva's knowledge of the path and so forth as distinct? It is said: because omniscience itself is the attainment of the fruit together with its cause, it is in reference to the Buddha, the Blessed One...
<leaf-break/>
...will be shown to be the aspect. If you ask for what purpose it is the cause: the passage "having closely examined" was spoken. Having closely examined all phenomena as emptiness through the various aspects of its object and aspects just explained, there is no discouragement because there is no attachment. Because of being endowed with reasoning, there is no fear. Furthermore, that which enters reality without error is the "Peak," and by realizing the divisions of small, medium, and great, the hearing of any enlightenment such as that of a Hearer is shown to be the proximity of all enlightenment and the Bodhisattva; it is shown to be the cause. After the Peak comes "Patience"; because it is the great Dharma patience characterized by the absence of lower realms, in order to show the object of having become patient, the passage beginning with "If" was spoken. "If one courses without knowing" means coursing without realizing selflessness. "Investigation" is conceptualization. "Coursing in signs" is coursing in the opposite. Thus, not knowing the nature of reality and being attached to form from the general characteristic of form down to consciousness—that is because it is harmed by valid cognition, like the perception of a mirage and so forth. "Coursing in the signs of an object"—thus it is connected. So it will be shown. Likewise, if one investigates the five aggregates such as form as "empty" and is attached to that, and if one courses without realizing the nature of phenomena, then at that time, being attached to "emptiness"...
pages.66:
...because that is also harmed by valid cognition, it is "coursing in signs." Likewise, after being attached to the nature of existence and non-existence, the Bodhisattva who courses in the opposite of that courses in the state which is the very birthless state; because it is the support for the path of seeing and so forth, it is the state; coursing without clinging to it and without attachment is the practice. Therefore, objectifying form and so forth characterized by the absence of nature while having abandoned nature entirely is the practice; it is shown to be the object. If you ask what its aspect is, the passage beginning with "That which is form..." was spoken. One who courses without a state because of birthlessness: the absence of everything from form to consciousness means one does not course in the attachment of grasping and does not experience it. Because there is no grasped, the Bodhisattva who courses without objectifying the grasper is again said to be "coursing"; thus they do not objectify and do not realize. Because of objectifying the nature of the wisdom of form and so forth as being without nature, one is completely unshakable by all aspects and signs; thus it is called "teaching wisdom." By that, the transformation is shown. If you ask for what purpose it is the cause: the passage beginning with "The wise one without birth" was spoken. Likewise, that wise one who realizes the objects and aspects as birthless, having realized the divisions of small, medium, and great patience, has a nature of one-pointed mental concentration...
<leaf-break/>
A "child" <note>Sanskrit: bala</note> is one in whom the path of the Aryas has not been born. Its "sign" is in accordance with reasoning. These phenomena as they appear are "existent." According to reasoning as it actually is, they are "non-existent." Furthermore, that which is to be abandoned is the basis of affliction. Ignorance itself is the first object of the conceptualization of the grasped; it acts in accordance with affliction. "Acting" means placing, just as one places what is to be purified. Likewise, what is to be adopted is the second object of the conceptualization of the grasped, based on the antidote; it is reasoning, and it is placed in accordance with conceptualization. Having thus established the conceptualization of the grasped, from this point onwards those two, together with the object of attachment, are shown to be meditated upon as false, like an illusion; thus the passage beginning with "knowledge and ignorance" was spoken. These two, knowledge and ignorance, are phenomena that do not exist as form and so forth because they are not born in reality; they are imputed as "knowledge" and "ignorance" by children through the power of manifest pride. Any Bodhisattva who knows this through the sequence of hearing and so forth emerges; by truly entering from the bond of error, they emerge. To show the first conceptualization of the grasper after the two conceptualizations of the grasped, the passage beginning with "Who" was spoken. Any Bodhisattva who, through the power of reasoning, [realizes] the aggregates as a deceptive illusion, [overcomes] the conceptualization of grasping the five aggregates as having a nature of a substantially existent person...
<leaf-break/>
...it is so; because it is the cause of gradual attainment. Up to the phrase "it is the application <note>Sanskrit: prayoga</note>, the engagement in experience." In order for these four conceptualizations to be understood by the people to be tamed who are close to the cycle [of existence], the Blessed One previously explained them in detail by dividing them according to objects, speaking of nine aspects for each. However, here the essentials are summarized and shown; there is no need for a detailed explanation, and the Blessed One, considering that the division by objects in the *One Hundred Thousand Lines* was not the primary focus here, made the division of the bases of the objects in terms of the portions of definite differentiation. The division of the conceptualizations made in terms of the vision of the peak realization and the path of meditation is another matter. Because this is the essence, from that characteristic which exists by mutually excluding [other things], there are no other aggregates; one should understand the subsequent ones in the same way, following the two previously explained conceptualizations of the grasped and the conceptualizations of the grasper. That shows the embracing by the nature of the spiritual friend <note>Sanskrit: kalyanamitra</note> and skill in methods. Because the previous explanation becomes specific through that power, the passage beginning with "Virtuous" was spoken. Because they are a person who teaches the Dharma without departing from the two truths and causes the attainment of the result of a happy migration, they are a "spiritual friend." To be endowed with that is "together with." After generating the knowledge of hearing and so forth through that very thing, "the one with discernment" is reasoning...

The deity of the ocean was exceedingly joyful. He offered many jewels to that <term>Upasaka</term> <gloss>lay devotee</gloss> and also sent excellent jewels to the Buddha and the <term>Sangha</term> <gloss>monastic community</gloss>. After the lay devotee and the merchants were satisfied with the riches, they returned safely to their own land. At that time, the lay devotee and about five hundred merchants came to where the Buddha was staying. They prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One with their heads touching the ground. Each of them held jewels, and they offered both their own gifts and those sent by the deity of the ocean to the Buddha and the Sangha. They knelt on the ground with palms pressed together and addressed the Blessed One: We also wish to go forth into the teachings of the Teacher. As soon as the Blessed One said, "Come, monks," their hair and beards fell away of their own accord, and they became monks wearing the dharma robes. Then the Blessed One taught them the Dharma in various ways, and by opening their minds, all their desires were exhausted, and they became <term>Arhats</term> <gloss>perfected ones who have attained liberation</gloss>. The great assembly rejoiced and were delighted by what the Blessed One had spoken.

This is the fifth chapter, The Questions of the Ocean Deity.

Book Two.

The chapter titled Gangadara, Son of a Deity.

Thus have I heard at one time. The Blessed One was staying in the Bamboo Grove at the Kalandaka site. At that time, in that country, there was a very great minister.

<leaf-break/>

addressed him in this way: A great minister in Rajgir is requesting a son from me. He has vowed that if his wish is fulfilled, he will offer worship and services. But if his wish is not fulfilled, he will destroy this shrine and make it unsightly. Since he will certainly act according to his vow, I pray to you, Shakra, King of the Gods, please grant him a son. Shakra replied: This is indeed very difficult, but I see a cause for it now. At that time, there was a son of a deity whose five virtues were fading and who was close to death. Shakra said to him: You are near the end of your life. When you pass away, you must be born as the son of that minister. The son of the deity replied: I have faith in going forth and practicing the holy Dharma. If I am born into a high and great family, it will be difficult to go forth. It would be easier if I were born into an ordinary family. Shakra spoke again: O deity, be born there, and if you have faith in going forth, I will assist you. After that son of the deity passed away from that realm, he was conceived in the womb of the minister’s wife. Later, when he was born, he was handsome, beautiful to behold, and excellent. He was shown to the fortune-tellers. The fortune-tellers examined him and asked, "From where was this boy first obtained?" When they replied, "He was requested from the deity of the river Ganges," the boy was given the name Gangadara <gloss>Gift of the Ganges</gloss>. Later, when he had reached maturity, he spoke to his parents.

The flower garland is given. By saying *Om vajra pashe ho* <gloss>Om, Vajra noose, ho!</gloss>, the blindfold is removed and the mandala is shown. Then, for the bestowal of the Vase Empowerment: the water in the skull cup and the water for the disciple are purified into the state of emptiness. From the state of emptiness, from the syllable *Hum* and a vajra, the deity Akshobhya and consort are generated, and the wisdom beings <term>jnanasattva</term> dissolve into them. The water becomes the melted essence of the union of the male and female deities of the empowerment substance. Then, the disciple makes a request to the Buddha, the Vajra of Awakening. A skull cup filled with the mind of awakening <term>bodhicitta</term> and the vase of nectar are placed on the disciple's head: "Today I shall bestow upon you the empowerment of the Vajra Hero Vase. So that you may become a Vajra Hero, receive this Vase Empowerment!"

<leaf-break/>

The Crown Empowerment is obtained. The stains of pride and miserliness are purified. The aggregate of feeling is transformed in its place. The Wisdom of Equality is actualized. Having become Ratnasambhava, one is empowered for his enlightened activities. Then, the disciple and a vajra are generated as Padma and Vajra, the male and female Lotus-Vajra. The vajra is handed over: "Today I shall bestow upon you the empowerment of the Lotus Hero Vajra. So that you may become a Lotus Hero, receive this Vajra Empowerment! *Padma Abhisheñca Hri* <gloss>Lotus Empowerment Hri</gloss>." The Vajra Empowerment is obtained. The stain of attachment is purified. The aggregate of perception is transformed in its place. The Discriminating Wisdom is actualized. Having become Amitabha, one is empowered to accomplish his enlightened activities. Then, the disciple and a bell...

<leaf-break/>

*Buddha Abhisheñca Om* <gloss>Buddha Empowerment Om</gloss>. "O Great Glorious One, you are given the secret vajra name [Name]." As they were born in their respective families, the Water Empowerment is bestowed. The Name Empowerment is obtained. The stain of ignorance is purified. The aggregate of form is transformed. The Mirror-like Wisdom is manifested. Having become Vairocana, one is empowered for his enlightened activities. In that way, by obtaining the five empowerments, the five objects of abandonment—the five ignorances—are abandoned. Because the five awareness-wisdoms are obtained, these are the Empowerments of Awareness. Then, the disciple is generated from the syllable *Hum* and a vajra as Vajrasattva and consort. The master says: *Om sarva tathagata siddha vajra samaya tishtha esha tvam dharayami om hi hi hi hum* <gloss>Om, may the accomplishment of all the Tathagatas, the Vajra Pledge, remain! I hold this for you! Om Hi Hi Hi Hum</gloss>. Placing the vajra in the right hand, it is held to the heart. The Vajra...
</translation>

<translation page="8">
*Om hri hri ha hum hum phat vajra abhisheñca hum* <gloss>Om Hri Hri Ha Hum Hum Phat, Vajra Empowerment Hum</gloss>. "Just as the Great Offering was granted, so that I also may be thoroughly protected, today I entrust myself to the Vajra of Space." The Water Empowerment is obtained. The stain of hatred is purified. The aggregate of consciousness is transformed. The Wisdom of the Dharmadhatu is actualized, and one becomes Akshobhya, empowered for his enlightened activities. Then, from the disciple and the crown, and from the syllable *Am* and a jewel, the Jewel-Vajra male and female are generated, and the wisdom beings are invited as before. Then, the diadem is handed over: "Today I shall bestow upon you the empowerment of the Jewel Hero Diadem. So that you may become a Jewel Hero, receive this Diadem Empowerment!" At the end of the seven-syllable mantra, say *Ratna abhisheñca tram* <gloss>Jewel Empowerment Tram</gloss> while placing it on the head...

<leaf-break/>

From the syllable *Tam* and a sword, the Karma-Vajra male and female are generated. Then the bell is handed over: "Today I shall bestow upon you the empowerment of the Karma Hero Bell. So that you may become a Karma Hero, receive this Bell Empowerment! *Karma abhisheñca a* <gloss>Karma Empowerment A</gloss>." The Bell Empowerment is obtained. The stain of jealousy is purified. The aggregate of mental formations is transformed. The All-Accomplishing Wisdom is manifested. Having become Amoghasiddhi, meditate that you are empowered for his infinite activities.
