<translation page="15">
The winds move in this way: the ten channels and ten winds cause all seventy-two thousand channels to be pervaded. Furthermore, from the left channel and left nostril, the winds of space, wind, fire, water, and earth move through the process of generation. From the right channel and right nostril, the winds of earth, water, fire, wind, and space move through the process of absorption. 
Their colors are also: green for space, black for wind, red for fire, white for water, and yellow for earth. 
Regarding the path and measure of their flow: the earth wind flows from the lower part of both nostrils to a distance of twelve finger-widths externally, and four finger-widths below the navel internally. The water wind flows from the side of the nasal septum thirteen finger-widths externally, and three finger-widths below the navel internally. The fire wind flows from the outer side of the nose fourteen finger-widths externally, and two finger-widths below the navel internally. The wind wind flows from the upper part of the nose fifteen finger-widths externally, and turns back internally from the navel <note>original: "pema" meaning lotus</note> itself. The wisdom wind flows at the end of the earth mandala...

<leaf-break/>

...the mandalas are these. According to that, during the sixty <term>chutsoe</term> <gloss>60-minute Tibetan hours</gloss> of a single day, there are twenty-one thousand six hundred inhalations and exhalations. For each of the twelve petals of the navel channel, there is a "great shift" or one <term>dujor</term> <gloss>zodiacal timing</gloss> consisting of one thousand eight hundred breaths. Since it flows for five <term>chutsoe</term> each, there are twelve shifts. 
When it moves through the six left channel-petals, the wind flows from the left nostril. When it moves through the six right channel-petals, the wind flows from the right nostril; this occurs by way of shifting between left and right for each <term>dujor</term>. In the transition between shifting from left to right and right to left, fifty-six and a quarter breaths move within the central <term>Avadhuti</term> channel. At that time, the wind flows equally through both nostrils. The central channel breaths for one full day total six hundred and seventy-five. 
As stated in the <term>Abbreviated Empowerment Tantra</term> <note>original: "Wang Dor-ten"</note>: At the precise transition when the <term>dujor</term> arises, it flows equally from the central channel; fifty-six with a quarter. In short, O Lord of Men, of the seventy-two thousand channels of inhalation and exhalation, six hundred and seventy-five extra occur during the night.

<leaf-break/>

...it is spoken of in relation to Venus, Saturn, and the "Long-Tailed One" <gloss>comets or Ketu</gloss>. Therefore, at this stage, one should bind those upper planets, and afterwards, the three lower planets should also be bound. 
First, regarding the examination of the place for accomplishment, the <term>Root Tantra</term> states: Where the protector of the land is righteous, where the people live in happiness, and where the mountains are free of conflict: there one should begin the practice. 
As it is said, in a place without civil strife or fighting, where the paths of humans and non-humans do not cross, one should gather the necessary provisions while avoiding the "wrong livelihoods" related to the Guru and the temple. The meditation cell should be naturally dark, with the interior designed like a series of tiered steps. In short, it should have a high ceiling, be well-plastered, and have a triple-layered entrance so that not even a needle-point of light enters. Sitting there on a comfortable cushion, one should generate the supreme Mind of Enlightenment <note>Bodhicitta</note>. Practice the <term>Guru Yoga</term> and offer fervent prayers. Then, initially, at the time when the life-force descends into the right channel...
</translation>

<translation page="16">
...when it descends, it is equivalent to the earth wind. When it descends at the end of the space wind, it is equivalent to the space wind. 
The functions of the ten winds mentioned previously are as follows: The life-sustaining wind, which has the nature of the Moon and Sun, provides support. The downward-clearing wind draws down the food and drink of the six tastes. The equally-abiding wind equalizes the essence of the seven constituents. The upward-moving wind governs the "naga," jumping, speaking, and so forth, as well as dancing and walking. The pervading wind governs jumping, running, opening, and movement. The "naga" wind causes belching. The "tortoise" wind causes the contraction of the feet and hands. The "lizard" wind causes all anger and agitation. The "Devadatta" wind causes yawning. The "Dhananjaya" wind ensures the dead body does not decompose. 
Regarding the life-sustaining wind, the <term>Abbreviated Empowerment Tantra</term> states: The gradual flow of the <term>chutsoe</term> is three hundred and sixty breaths; those eighteen hundred breaths flow in the previous <term>chutsoe</term>. For the sixty <term>chutsoe</term> of day and night, the body...

<leaf-break/>

...the essence of these is the wind and the <term>Alaya-vijnana</term> <gloss>all-ground consciousness</gloss>, which is the Mind of Enlightenment. The former is the support, and the latter is that which is supported. 
From failing to bind these, the "four states of cyclic existence" and the "four great leaking gates of cyclic existence" arise. Because one is liberated from cyclic existence by binding them in sequence, it is called "binding." Where should they be bound? In the expanse of space. They are bound by the two yogas of the space of darkness and the space of light. In what manner are they bound? Through stability; they are bound without movement, so that the object and the subject do not enter into one another. 
Here, "the planets" refers to the doors of the senses. According to the <term>Stainless Light</term> <note>Vimalaprabha</note>: Here, the channels of feces, urine, semen, the mouth, the right eye, the left eye, the right nostril, the left nostril, the right ear, and the left ear are respectively: the Moon, the Sun, Rahu, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Ketu...

<leaf-break/>

...one should meditate with the mind placed in space. It is not at the time when the wind flows into the left channel, because that generates space and so forth. 
Furthermore, regarding the key points of the body: assume the cross-legged posture. Straighten the spine. Bind the two hands in the "vajra fist" and press the channels of the two thighs. Spread the two shoulders back slightly. Bend the neck slightly so the chin presses against the throat. Look upward without moving with the "wrathful gaze of the wheel-holder." 
Because the body, mind, and wind are dependent on one another, if the key points of the body are distorted, the key points of the wind and mind will also be distorted. Therefore, if one knows how to assume the cross-legged posture well, the secret downward-clearing wind and the wind-wind are bound. By placing the fists on the tops of the thighs and straightening the abdomen, the heat-equalizing wind is bound. By spreading the shoulders like the wings of a vulture and keeping the chest neither too projected nor too sunken, the life-holding water-wind in the heart is bound. By pressing the chin against the throat like a noble horse being reined in...
</translation>

It provides specific instructions on the yogic postures and sensory "bindings" necessary to synchronize the physical body with the subtle mind for spiritual liberation.
</summary>

...with the Good One. It was held in the Abode of Beautifully Arrayed. Then, in the abode of <term>Alakavati</term> <gloss>the realm of Vajrapani</gloss>, Sarvavid-Vairochana held this, and it ripened into the five families. After he passed, through my holding of it, the teachings were completed. Based on this, the one thousand and two Buddhas of the Fortunate Aeon will certainly appear. It causes the ripening of beings born from miraculous birth, eggs, heat, and the womb. From this very teaching of the <term>Vinaya</term> <gloss>monastic discipline</gloss>, the twelve cycles of the wheel of Dharma arise. Its thirty-six deeds, based on Body, Speech, and Mind, are granted to the beings to be tamed. After I pass into <term>Nirvana</term> <gloss>extinction of suffering</gloss>, in the western land of Oddiyana, to the divine lady of Lake Kosha, a fatherless son, Vajrapani, will appear. He will uphold the sacred teachings. His successor in the West, the fortunate child of a Brahmin named Manjushrimitra, will uphold them for seventy-five years. After him, a fortunate one from the family of householders in the land of Shosha, named Shri Singha, will be the holder. His successor, from a commoner family, Jnanasutra, will uphold this very teaching. His successor, from a householder family, Vimalamitra will uphold them. After him, from a royal family, the <term>Nirmanakaya</term> <gloss>emanation body</gloss> with his attendants will uphold them. After him, in the form of a monk, Nyang Tingdzin Zangpo will uphold them. After him, Singhashvara will uphold them. After him, the <term>Bodhisattvas</term> <gloss>enlightenment beings</gloss> dwelling on the stages will uphold them. Below that, the emanation of Vajrapani, Vajraphala, will uphold it. After him, King Sengge Zangpo will be the holder. Below him, the scholar Pelzin. Below him, the yogi Traba. Below him, King Thri Ö. Below him, the monks Pel and Yon. Then, Lodrö Chok will uphold it. After that, the <term>Dakini</term> <gloss>sky-goer</gloss> Pelzinma, having held this very teaching, will cause it to flourish during the time of the ten-year lifespan. Then, it will not remain but return to its own place. This heart-essence of the teachings...

<leaf-break/>

...will be. Although it cannot be fully described, the end of the teachings is inconceivable; for now, it is indicated by words. As for the body and branches of the <term>Tantra</term>, there are two hundred and fifty instructions on the arrangement within the body. First, through clear certainty, for the instructions on various arrangements, there are seventy requests, making one hundred instructions on arrangement. This completes the body itself. Its branches are six hundred and ten. The bodies and branches of the higher ones are completed. When the body is completed, the instructions are kept secret. The second body is shown as the arrangement of gathered abodes; to the twenty-eight requests, there are thirty-one on the arrangement of gathered abodes. By that, the body itself is completed. Its branches are two hundred and ten. By that, the second body and its branches are completed. The third body is based on the twenty-two requests; there are fifty-eight on the arrangement of primordial wisdom. The branches themselves are two hundred. The third body and branches are completed. For the fourth body and branches, there are twenty-one requests, and thirty-two on the arrangement of the <term>Dharmata</term> <gloss>nature of reality</gloss>. The branches are sixty-four. For the fifth body and branches, there are eleven requests; there are thirty-two on the arrangement of view and meditation. Its branches are sixty-four. The fifth body and branches are completed. For the sixth body and branches, written for the eight requests, there are eighteen on the arrangement of the <term>Kayas</term> <gloss>Buddha bodies</gloss>. Its branches are thirty-two. The sixth body and branches are completed. The desires of the elements arise like this: from the general and specific karmic actions, the foundational ground of the karma of sentient beings depends on the external elements. Through this, karma, nourishment, the sense faculties, retinue, and birth are asserted to be completed. The sequence of the internal elements of karma is: through earth, the four parts of the body are made; through development, it is asserted as the ripening of earth. Through fire, the entire body is heated; through development, it is asserted as the ripening of warmth. Through wind, the entire body is supported; through development, it is asserted as the ripening of breath. The specific meanings of those sounds...

<leaf-break/>

...first arranged. From the first formless internal upper realm, the form realms and the Clear Light appear. In the gradual desire realms, from the stainless moon and the clearly illuminating sun, the world realms spread. There are the four gradual levels of "Others' Emanations" and so forth. Then there are the abodes of the demi-gods, and the humans of the four continents in sequence. Along with the self of afflictions, the abodes of the lower realms are formed in sequence. In the migrations of the six classes of beings, they are formed internally, and their body size and lifespan are many according to the weight of their karma. Each individual's abode and merit are situated in accordance with their continent. The meaning concerns destruction, formation, staying, and emptiness, along with birth, old age, sickness, and death, within the cycle of existence itself. The shift of time is like this: from the initial incalculable time until the final ten-year lifespan, there is the upward growth and downward waning. Through the junction of the three minor aeons of disease, famine, and weapons, sixty stages pass. Then, through seven destructions by fire and seven by water, when fourteen are thus completed, the remainder is destruction by wind. Just as there are sixty stages of staying, the duration of destruction is the same; it remains empty for sixty stages. Thus, one hundred, and one hundred and ten is asserted as the first duration of an aeon. Thus, one hundred and eighty is the second intermediate aeon. Such an announced duration is one Great Aeon. Thirty days make one month. When twelve of those are completed, it is asserted as one year. When seven hundred mornings and evenings are completed, it is asserted as three hundred and sixty days. By completing those, one year is formed; the days are divided by male and female activities. The months of autumn, spring, summer, and winter each proceed for three months and perform the spoken activities. The Mouse, Ox, Tiger, Hare, Dragon, Snake, Horse, Sheep, Monkey, Bird, Dog...

<translation page="9">
...and Pig, these twelve expand the calculations of the elements. For the yogi who knows the application of increasing and healing life, as well as the rites of the king and the practices, they will become equal to the sun and moon. For others, the practices of degrading, destroying, summoning, binding, striking vital points, transferring, and killing—if the yogi knows how to manipulate these, they will bring all beings under their power. The application for increasing and healing prosperity, and for maintaining or destroying abodes, should be undertaken by the yogi. There are twelve cycles of spreading, piercing, and balancing. For the four elements of earth, water, fire, and wind, there are three each, making twelve. Through the piercing of water, the sense faculties are gathered. Through its spreading, it causes disturbance. Through its balancing, it brings forth results. Through the piercing of earth, dust is produced. Through its spreading, the limbs are held. Through its balancing, the physical elements are perfected. Through the piercing of fire, disease is caused. Through its spreading, the state of the body is changed. Through its balancing, the elements are maintained. The piercing of wind protects the elements. Through its spreading, other activities are destroyed. Through its balancing, the wind-mind is gathered in the <term>Avadhuti</term> <gloss>central channel</gloss>. This is the limit of the three functions. In various times of the water's piercing, through the meeting of leakages and flows, whatever is not accomplished will be destroyed. Through the two spreadings, disease occurs. Through balancing, the applications of medicinal elixirs are accomplished. Fire and wind together destroy the aggregates. Through spreading, all activities are accomplished, while through balancing, the activities of delusion reach their end. With water and fire, the objective is excellently accomplished. Through spreading, it will enter into others. Through balancing, life and prosperity are accomplished. With earth and wind, pacification is accomplished. Through spreading, enrichment and suppression are performed. Through balancing, the activities of wrathful magic are accomplished. Through spreading...

<leaf-break/>

...the <term>Nirmanakaya</term> <gloss>emanation body</gloss> is also certainly accomplished. The sound of earth is cool and heavy; it possesses the melodic voice of Great Brahma. If one always listens to and practices this, the <term>Sambhogakaya</term> <gloss>enjoyment body</gloss> is certainly accomplished. The sound of fire is long and undulating; it shows the melodic speech of Great Vishnu. Whoever practices listening to this will certainly obtain the qualities of the <term>Dharmakaya</term> <gloss>truth body</gloss>. The sound of wind is piercing and fierce, the speech of the application of the King of Birds <note>Garuda</note>. If one knows how to always recite this, the common trainings of Body and Speech are achieved. Thus, the meaning of the sounds of the four elements is certainly applied to external time. The flow of spring, summer, and autumn, through water, earth, fire, and wind, is applied to specific times in sequence; if the yogi aligns this with the body, there is no doubt of accomplishment. As for the end of common worldly activities: those who wish to fly rely on pills. Those who wish for invisibility should settle the mind; by placing both body and mind within the web of the empty <term>Bindu</term> <gloss>essential drop</gloss>, it is accomplished. Those who wish to obtain unimpeded transparency should hold the wind itself and dwell in the <term>Bindu</term>. When awareness is like a mist, it should be extracted from the Brahma-opening. Those who wish to triumph over weapons and poison should focus the mind on the four elements; by purifying the later ones and training well, they will certainly be accomplished. To triumph over dogs, bears, and wolves, one should vocalize the four elements; by performing the four dependent originations, one will triumph over them. Those who wish to be liberated from the eight fears should hold a wheel-drawing on the crown; if one meditates on the wind, one will also triumph over those. For those who wish to achieve clear vision, by using the paper-preparation called "Khati," well-prepared and always reciting the letters of clarity, even the three realms will appear clearly. In war, trade, and marriage, for those who wish to be victorious, by taking the time and direction of the elements and acting without error, they will certainly succeed without doubt. Whosoever...

<leaf-break/>

...develops the experience. Through the experience of one's own system, if one becomes familiar with it, even the <term>Heruka</term> <gloss>wrathful deity</gloss> is accomplished. The scent of wind is the place of training. By combining the natural state and activities, if one meditates clearly on the sequence of certain gathering, the bodies of the five families will certainly be accomplished. Furthermore, by training in the sequence of taste and touch, there is no doubt that whatever body one desires will be accomplished. For whoever meditates on the yoga of sleep, this makes ignorance into the path. External time is from the mouth; by purifying the yoga of the body and exhausting the channels within, that is the vital point. Internal time is by its own nature; by training the yoga of speech and cutting the flow of expressions, that is the vital point. Secret time is also the fourth; by training the yoga of the mind and becoming familiar with sleep, that is the vital point. Through the four times of suchness, having certainly gathered body, speech, and mind, mix the Great Clear Light with sleep. By thus becoming familiar, the yogi will certainly be joined to the three <term>Kayas</term>. If one takes the dream vital point as the path, one must first perform the preliminaries and then strike the vital point. Based on the signs of having trained in the preliminaries of body, speech, and mind, one must certainly grasp the three: constancy, overwhelming, and habitual tendencies. Then, at the time of striking the vital point: purify, cause to arise, cut, stir, extract, and cast into the vital point. By performing the vital point of reversing the center, the ten karmic dreams are exhausted, and the delusion of habitual tendencies is uprooted and cast away. At this time, through one's own diligence, the superior is known from the roots and the intermediate from the activities. The final is certain to be transformed; these are the many initial dreams. For the superior, the forgotten speech is finally blocked. For the intermediate, it is very clear, and then the final clarity is transformed. These reach the measure. If the person's own mind does not pass into excess, but meditates on non-conceptuality, it will certainly pass through; when it arrives at the natural state, that is one's own ground. The sequence of previous training depends on the four actual causes...

<summary>This page describes advanced yogic practices involving the manipulation of elements to achieve both mundane powers (like invisibility and victory in battle) and supreme realization. It concludes with specific instructions on the yogas of sleep and dreams to transform ignorance and habitual patterns into the Clear Light and the three Buddha bodies.</summary>
<keywords>Yoga, Elements, Siddhi, Clear Light, Sleep Yoga, Dream Yoga, Three Kayas, Heruka</keywords></translation>

He will uphold the sacred teachings. His successor in the West, the fortunate child of a Brahmin named Manjushrimitra, will uphold them for seventy-five years. After him, a fortunate one from the family of householders in the land of Shosha, named Shri Singha, will be the holder. His successor, from a commoner family, Jnanasutra, will uphold this very teaching. His successor, from a householder family, Vimalamitra will uphold them. After him, from a royal family, the <term>Nirmanakaya</term> <gloss>emanation body</gloss> with his attendants will uphold them. After him, in the form of a monk, Nyang Tingdzin Zangpo will uphold them. After him, Singhashvara will uphold them. After him, the <term>Bodhisattvas</term> <gloss>enlightenment beings</gloss> dwelling on the stages will uphold them. Below that, the emanation of Vajrapani, Vajraphala, will uphold it. After him, King Sengge Zangpo will be the holder. Below him, the scholar Pelzin. Below him, the yogi Traba. Below him, King Thri Ö. Below him, the monks Pel and Yon. Then, Lodrö Chok will uphold it. After that, the <term>Dakini</term> <gloss>sky-goer</gloss> Pelzinma, having held this very teaching, will cause it to flourish during the time of the ten-year lifespan. Then, it will not remain but return to its own place. This heart-essence of the teachings...

<leaf-break/>

...will be. Although it cannot be fully described, the end of the teachings is inconceivable; for now, it is indicated by words. As for the body and branches of the <term>Tantra</term>, there are two hundred and fifty instructions on the arrangement within the body. First, through clear certainty, for the instructions on various arrangements, there are seventy requests, making one hundred instructions on arrangement. This completes the body itself. Its branches are six hundred and ten. The bodies and branches of the higher ones are completed. When the body is completed, the instructions are kept secret. The second body is shown as the arrangement of gathered abodes; to the twenty-eight requests, there are thirty-one on the arrangement of gathered abodes. By that, the body itself is completed. Its branches are two hundred and ten. By that, the second body and its branches are completed. The third body is based on the twenty-two requests; there are fifty-eight on the arrangement of primordial wisdom. The branches themselves are two hundred. The third body and branches are completed. For the fourth body and branches, there are twenty-one requests, and thirty-two on the arrangement of the <term>Dharmata</term> <gloss>nature of reality</gloss>. The branches are sixty-four. For the fifth body and branches, there are eleven requests; there are thirty-two on the arrangement of view and meditation. Its branches are sixty-four. The fifth body and branches are completed. For the sixth body and branches, written for the eight requests, there are eighteen on the arrangement of the <term>Kayas</term> <gloss>Buddha bodies</gloss>. Its branches are thirty-two. The sixth body and branches are completed. The desires of the elements arise like this: from the general and specific karmic actions, the foundational ground of the karma of sentient beings depends on the external elements. Through this, karma, nourishment, the sense faculties, retinue, and birth are asserted to be completed. The sequence of the internal elements of karma is: through earth, the four parts of the body are made; through development, it is asserted as the ripening of earth. Through fire, the entire body is heated; through development, it is asserted as the ripening of warmth. Through wind, the entire body is supported; through development, it is asserted as the ripening of breath. The specific meanings of those sounds...

<leaf-break/>

...first arranged. From the first formless internal upper realm, the form realms and the Clear Light appear. In the gradual desire realms, from the stainless moon and the clearly illuminating sun, the world realms spread. There are the four gradual levels of "Others' Emanations" and so forth. Then there are the abodes of the demi-gods, and the humans of the four continents in sequence. Along with the self of afflictions, the abodes of the lower realms are formed in sequence. In the migrations of the six classes of beings, they are formed internally, and their body size and lifespan are many according to the weight of their karma. Each individual's abode and merit are situated in accordance with their continent. The meaning concerns destruction, formation, staying, and emptiness, along with birth, old age, sickness, and death, within the cycle of existence itself. The shift of time is like this: from the initial incalculable time until the final ten-year lifespan, there is the upward growth and downward waning. Through the junction of the three minor aeons of disease, famine, and weapons, sixty stages pass. Then, through seven destructions by fire and seven by water, when fourteen are thus completed, the remainder is destruction by wind. Just as there are sixty stages of staying, the duration of destruction is the same; it remains empty for sixty stages. Thus, one hundred, and one hundred and ten is asserted as the first duration of an aeon. Thus, one hundred and eighty is the second intermediate aeon. Such an announced duration is one Great Aeon. Thirty days make one month. When twelve of those are completed, it is asserted as one year. When seven hundred mornings and evenings are completed, it is asserted as three hundred and sixty days. By completing those, one year is formed; the days are divided by male and female activities. The months of autumn, spring, summer, and winter each proceed for three months and perform the spoken activities. The Mouse, Ox, Tiger, Hare, Dragon, Snake, Horse, Sheep, Monkey, Bird, Dog...

<summary>Page 8 details the lineage of the Great Perfection teachings from celestial realms to historical masters in India and Tibet. It then provides a technical breakdown of the tantra's structure, the formation of the physical body from elements, and the cosmology of world cycles and time measurements.</summary>
<keywords>Lineage, Vajrapani, Vimalamitra, Aeon, Elements, Cosmology, Tantra Structure, Calendar</keywords>
pages.9:
...and Pig, these twelve expand the calculations of the elements. For the yogi who knows the application of increasing and healing life, as well as the rites of the king and the practices, they will become equal to the sun and moon. For others, the practices of degrading, destroying, summoning, binding, striking vital points, transferring, and killing—if the yogi knows how to manipulate these, they will bring all beings under their power. The application for increasing and healing prosperity, and for maintaining or destroying abodes, should be undertaken by the yogi. There are twelve cycles of spreading, piercing, and balancing. For the four elements of earth, water, fire, and wind, there are three each, making twelve. Through the piercing of water, the sense faculties are gathered. Through its spreading, it causes disturbance. Through its balancing, it brings forth results. Through the piercing of earth, dust is produced. Through its spreading, the limbs are held. Through its balancing, the physical elements are perfected. Through the piercing of fire, disease is caused. Through its spreading, the state of the body is changed. Through its balancing, the elements are maintained. The piercing of wind protects the elements. Through its spreading, other activities are destroyed. Through its balancing, the wind-mind is gathered in the <term>Avadhuti</term> <gloss>central channel</gloss>. This is the limit of the three functions. In various times of the water's piercing, through the meeting of leakages and flows, whatever is not accomplished will be destroyed. Through the two spreadings, disease occurs. Through balancing, the applications of medicinal elixirs are accomplished. Fire and wind together destroy the aggregates. Through spreading, all activities are accomplished, while through balancing, the activities of delusion reach their end. With water and fire, the objective is excellently accomplished. Through spreading, it will enter into others. Through balancing, life and prosperity are accomplished. With earth and wind, pacification is accomplished. Through spreading, enrichment and suppression are performed. Through balancing, the activities of wrathful magic are accomplished. Through spreading...

<leaf-break/>

...the <term>Nirmanakaya</term> <gloss>emanation body</gloss> is also certainly accomplished. The sound of earth is cool and heavy; it possesses the melodic voice of Great Brahma. If one always listens to and practices this, the <term>Sambhogakaya</term> <gloss>enjoyment body</gloss> is certainly accomplished. The sound of fire is long and undulating; it shows the melodic speech of Great Vishnu. Whoever practices listening to this will certainly obtain the qualities of the <term>Dharmakaya</term> <gloss>truth body</gloss>. The sound of wind is piercing and fierce, the speech of the application of the King of Birds <note>Garuda</note>. If one knows how to always recite this, the common trainings of Body and Speech are achieved. Thus, the meaning of the sounds of the four elements is certainly applied to external time. The flow of spring, summer, and autumn, through water, earth, fire, and wind, is applied to specific times in sequence; if the yogi aligns this with the body, there is no doubt of accomplishment. As for the end of common worldly activities: those who wish to fly rely on pills. Those who wish for invisibility should settle the mind; by placing both body and mind within the web of the empty <term>Bindu</term> <gloss>essential drop</gloss>, it is accomplished. Those who wish to obtain unimpeded transparency should hold the wind itself and dwell in the <term>Bindu</term>. When awareness is like a mist, it should be extracted from the Brahma-opening. Those who wish to triumph over weapons and poison should focus the mind on the four elements; by purifying the later ones and training well, they will certainly be accomplished. To triumph over dogs, bears, and wolves, one should vocalize the four elements; by performing the four dependent originations, one will triumph over them. Those who wish to be liberated from the eight fears should hold a wheel-drawing on the crown; if one meditates on the wind, one will also triumph over those. For those who wish to achieve clear vision, by using the paper-preparation called "Khati," well-prepared and always reciting the letters of clarity, even the three realms will appear clearly. In war, trade, and marriage, for those who wish to be victorious, by taking the time and direction of the elements and acting without error, they will certainly succeed without doubt. Whosoever...

<leaf-break/>

...develops the experience. Through the experience of one's own system, if one becomes familiar with it, even the <term>Heruka</term> <gloss>wrathful deity</gloss> is accomplished. The scent of wind is the place of training. By combining the natural state and activities, if one meditates clearly on the sequence of certain gathering, the bodies of the five families will certainly be accomplished. Furthermore, by training in the sequence of taste and touch, there is no doubt that whatever body one desires will be accomplished. For whoever meditates on the yoga of sleep, this makes ignorance into the path. External time is from the mouth; by purifying the yoga of the body and exhausting the channels within, that is the vital point. Internal time is by its own nature; by training the yoga of speech and cutting the flow of expressions, that is the vital point. Secret time is also the fourth; by training the yoga of the mind and becoming familiar with sleep, that is the vital point. Through the four times of suchness, having certainly gathered body, speech, and mind, mix the Great Clear Light with sleep. By thus becoming familiar, the yogi will certainly be joined to the three <term>Kayas</term>. If one takes the dream vital point as the path, one must first perform the preliminaries and then strike the vital point. Based on the signs of having trained in the preliminaries of body, speech, and mind, one must certainly grasp the three: constancy, overwhelming, and habitual tendencies. Then, at the time of striking the vital point: purify, cause to arise, cut, stir, extract, and cast into the vital point. By performing the vital point of reversing the center, the ten karmic dreams are exhausted, and the delusion of habitual tendencies is uprooted and cast away. At this time, through one's own diligence, the superior is known from the roots and the intermediate from the activities. The final is certain to be transformed; these are the many initial dreams. For the superior, the forgotten speech is finally blocked. For the intermediate, it is very clear, and then the final clarity is transformed. These reach the measure. If the person's own mind does not pass into excess, but meditates on non-conceptuality, it will certainly pass through; when it arrives at the natural state, that is one's own ground. The sequence of previous training depends on the four actual causes...

<summary>This page describes advanced yogic practices involving the manipulation of elements to achieve both mundane powers (like invisibility and victory in battle) and supreme realization. It concludes with specific instructions on the yogas of sleep and dreams to transform ignorance and habitual patterns into the Clear Light and the three Buddha bodies.</summary>
<keywords>Yoga, Elements, Siddhi, Clear Light, Sleep Yoga, Dream Yoga, Three Kayas, Heruka</keywords>

Extending life, healing, accomplishment, and the great rituals of kings—if a yogi knows these applications, they will become equal to the sun and moon. Other activities such as degrading, destroying, summoning, binding, and striking the vital points, as well as transferring and killing—if a yogi knows how to manipulate these, they will bring all beings under their power. Increasing and healing the "Power-horse" <note>original: "dbang thang," referring to personal charisma or destiny</note>, and dealing with the staying and breaking of things—the yogi should engage in these applications when others have failed. There are twelve applications of "Diffusing, Piercing, and Balancing." For each of the four elements—earth, water, fire, and wind—there are three, making twelve. Through the "piercing" of water, the senses are withdrawn. Through its "diffusing," they are disturbed. From "balancing," the fruit is produced. Through the "piercing" of earth, the atoms are expelled. Through its "diffusing," the limbs are held. By "balancing," the bodily elements are perfected. Through the "piercing" of fire, sickness is caused. Through its "diffusing," the physical state is transformed. By "balancing," the elements are stabilized. The "piercing" of wind protects the elements. Through "diffusing," other activities are destroyed. By "balancing," the wind and mind are gathered into the <term>Avadhuti</term> <gloss>central channel</gloss>. These are the limits of the three actions. At various times of the "piercing" of water, if an impurity or leak is encountered, nothing will be accomplished and destruction will follow. Through the two types of "diffusing," sickness will arise. Through "balancing," the preparation of elixirs and medications will be accomplished. Fire and wind together destroy the aggregates. Through "diffusing," all activities are accomplished, and through "balancing," the ends of mistaken activities are reached. In water and fire, the purpose is perfectly accomplished. Through "diffusing," one enters into others. Through "balancing," life and power are accomplished. In earth and wind, pacification is accomplished. Through "diffusing," enrichment and suppression are performed. Through "balancing," wrathful activities are accomplished. The activities of wind and water degrade. Through "diffusing," all virtuous activities are accomplished. Through "balancing," one is victorious in battle. Earth and fire are accomplished through "increasing." Through "diffusing," the existing elements are accomplished. Through "balancing," the rituals of strength are accomplished. Through diffusing...

<leaf-break/>

...and the Nirmanakaya <note>emanation body</note> will certainly be accomplished. The sound of earth is cool and heavy; it possesses the melodic voice of Great Brahma. If one always listens to and practices this, the Sambhogakaya <note>enjoyment body</note> will certainly be accomplished. The sound of fire is long and undulating; it shows the melodic speech of Great Vishnu. Whoever practices listening to this will certainly obtain the qualities of the Dharmakaya <note>truth body</note>. The sound of wind is piercing and fierce; it is the yoga-speech of the King of Birds <note>Garuda</note>. If one knows how to recite this always, one should train in the commonality of the Body and Speech. Thus, the meaning of the sounds of the four elements should be applied with certainty to the external times. The flow of spring, summer, and autumn are linked to water, earth, fire, and wind. If these are applied with certainty to the times and synchronized with the yogi's body, there is no doubt they will be accomplished. Regarding the limits of common worldly activities: those who wish to fly rely on pills. Those who wish for invisibility should settle the mind; by placing both body and mind within the web of the "Empty Bindu" <note>original: "thig le stong pa"</note>, it is accomplished. Those who wish to obtain "Unimpeded Penetration" <note>original: "zang thal"</note> should hold the wind itself and dwell in the Bindu. Occasionally, when the consciousness is like a mist, it should be ejected from the "Opening of Brahma" <note>at the crown of the head</note>. Those who wish to be victorious over weapons and poison should focus the mind on the four elements; by purifying the later elements and practicing well, these will certainly be accomplished. To be victorious over dogs, bears, and wolves, one should vocalize the four elements; by performing the four dependent-links, one will be victorious over them. Those who wish to be liberated from the "eight fears" should hold a "hare-marked" disk <note>the moon</note> at the crown and meditate on the wind; this too will bring victory over them. Those who wish to accomplish "Eye-medicine" <note>original: "mig pun"</note> should use a paper preparation called "Khati." If it is well-prepared and the "Letters of Illumination" are constantly recited, even the three realms will appear clearly. Those who wish to be victorious in war, trade, or marriage should grasp the time and direction of the elements; if this is done without error, there is no doubt of success. Whatever...

<leaf-break/>

...develops the experience. By the "Light Experience" <note>original: "la ba'i nyams"</note> of one's own system, if one becomes familiar with it, even the Heruka will be accomplished. The "Scent of Wind" is the place of training. One should combine the natural state with activity; if one meditates clearly on the sequence of the "Certain Gathering," the Kayas of the Five Families will certainly be accomplished. Furthermore, by training in the sequence of the "One and Two Tastes," whatever Kaya one desires will be accomplished without a doubt. Whoever meditates on the "Yoga of Sleep" uses ignorance as the path. Regarding the "External Time": one should train the yogi's body in its skills from the <unclear>kha dag</unclear> <gloss>primordial purity</gloss> state; the key point is to exhaust the channels internally. Regarding the "Internal Time": by the natural state itself, one should train the yogi's speech in its skills; the key point is to cut the flow of expression. Regarding the "Secret Time" of the four: one should train the yogi's mind in its skills; the key point is familiarity with sleep. Through the four "Times of Reality" <note>original: "kho na nyid kྱི་དུས་"</note>, one definitely gathers the body, speech, and mind and mixes sleep with the Great Clear Light. If the yogi is familiar with this, they will certainly be joined to the Three Kayas. Regarding taking the key points of the Dream as the path: first, perform the preliminaries and strike the vital points. Preliminarily, based on the signs of having trained the body, speech, and mind, one should definitely grasp the three: "permanence," "overwhelming with brilliance," and "latent tendencies." Then, at the time of striking the vital points, through the points of "purifying," "causing," "cutting," "stirring," "extracting the essence," and "leaving it at the vital point," and through the "reversal of the mandala," the dreams of karma are exhausted, and the confusion of latent tendencies is uprooted and cast away. At this time, through one's own diligence, the best will know the channels and the intermediate will know the activities. The certain outcome is that they will be transformed; these are the many initial dreams. For the best, the "forgotten speech" is finally blocked. For the intermediate, it is very clear. For the lowest, it becomes clear through conservation and then transforms. These reach the standard. When a person's own mind does not overflow, and one meditates on non-conceptuality, it will certainly overflow; when it settles into its natural state, that is one's own ground. The sequence of previous training and the four actualities rely on their own causes...

<summary>This page describes various yogic applications and rituals tied to the elements, including methods for gaining power, healing, and achieving supernatural feats like invisibility. It also details the "Yoga of Sleep" and dream practices, explaining how to transform ignorance into the path and recognize the clear light during sleep.</summary>
<keywords>Yoga of Sleep, Dream Yoga, Elements, Supernatural feats, Clear Light, Five Buddha Families, Rituals, Bindu</keywords>
</translation>

...will become. Thus, though one cannot express it all, the end of the teachings is inconceivable; for now, it is merely indicated with words. As for the body and branches of the Tantra: the "body" consists of two hundred and fifty arrangements. First, through clear certainty, there are seventy requested instructions on the various arrangements of pith instructions; for the pith instructions on arrangement, there are one hundred and <unclear>1</unclear>. This completes the body itself. Its branches are six hundred and ten. By completing the previous body and branches, the body is finished and the pith instructions are kept secret. The "second body" is shown as follows: for the arrangement of the gathering of places, there are twenty-eight requested instructions; for the arrangement of the gathered places, there are thirty-one. By this, the body itself is completed. The branches are two hundred and <unclear>number</unclear>. By this, the second body and its branches are completed. The "third body" is supported as follows: there are twenty-two requested instructions, and fifty-eight arrangements of primordial wisdom. For the branches themselves, there are two hundred. The third body and branches are completed. The "fourth body" and branches: the requests are twenty-one, and the arrangements of the <term>Dharmata</term> <gloss>intrinsic nature</gloss> are thirty-two. The branches are sixty-four. The "fifth body" and branches: the requests are eleven, and the arrangements of view and meditation are thirty-two. Its branches are sixty-four. The fifth body and branches are completed. The "sixth body" and branches: for the eight written requests, there are sixteen arrangements of the <term>Kayas</term> <gloss>Buddha bodies</gloss>. Its branches are thirty-two. The sixth body and branches are completed. The desires of the elements arise as follows: from the specific karmas of the "General Crown," the earth is the support for the karma of sentient beings. By relying on the external elements, karma, nourishment, the senses, the retinue, and birth are asserted to be completed. The internal sequence of the elements' karma is: through the <note>water</note> the four parts of the body are made, and through its development, the "ripening of earth" is asserted. Through fire, the entire body is generated, and through that generation, the "ripening of heat" is asserted. Through wind, the entire body is supported, and through its development, the "ripening of breath" is asserted. The specific meanings of their sounds...

<leaf-break/>

...arranged first. Within the first formless realm, there are the form realms which are clear light. Successively, in the desire realm, there is the stainless moon and the sun which provides great illumination. From these, the world-realms spread. These are the four successive levels such as the "Emanation by Others" <note>original: "gzhan sprul"</note>. Then there are the abodes of the <term>Asuras</term> <gloss>demi-gods</gloss>, and the inhabitants of the four continents in succession. Along with the "I" of the afflictions, the abodes of the lower realms are formed in succession. Regarding the beings of the six classes, they are formed internally with various body sizes, lifespans, and activities according to their karma. Their respective places and merits are situated in accordance with the continents. The meaning is: destruction, formation, staying, and emptiness; birth, aging, sickness, and death; and the very cycle of existence. Through the joints of the three minor aeons—sickness, famine, and weapons—sixty stages pass. Then again, seven destructions by fire and seven by water occur. When these fourteen are finished, the remainder is destruction by wind. The staying for sixty such cycles and the duration of destruction are the same; for the duration of sixty, it remains empty. Thus, one hundred, one hundred and ten, and the duration are asserted as the first aeon. Thus, one hundred and eighty is the second intermediate aeon. The duration known as such is one great aeon. Thirty days make one month. The completion of twelve such months is asserted as one year. The completion of seven hundred mornings and evenings is asserted as three hundred and sixty days. By completing these, one year is formed; the distinction of days comes from the "male and female" actions. The months of autumn, spring, summer, and winter each last for three months, performing the activities of entry and speech. The rat, ox, tiger, hare, dragon, snake, horse, sheep, monkey, bird, dog...

...and the pig—through these twelve, the calculations of the elements are increased. Extending life, healing, accomplishment, and the great rituals of kings—if a yogi knows these applications, they will become equal to the sun and moon. Other activities such as degrading, destroying, summoning, binding, and striking the vital points, as well as transferring and killing—if a yogi knows how to manipulate these, they will bring all beings under their power. Increasing and healing the "Power-horse" <note>original: "dbang thang," referring to personal charisma or destiny</note>, and dealing with the staying and breaking of things—the yogi should engage in these applications when others have failed. There are twelve applications of "Diffusing, Piercing, and Balancing." For each of the four elements—earth, water, fire, and wind—there are three, making twelve. Through the "piercing" of water, the senses are withdrawn. Through its "diffusing," they are disturbed. From "balancing," the fruit is produced. Through the "piercing" of earth, the atoms are expelled. Through its "diffusing," the limbs are held. By "balancing," the bodily elements are perfected. Through the "piercing" of fire, sickness is caused. Through its "diffusing," the physical state is transformed. By "balancing," the elements are stabilized. The "piercing" of wind protects the elements. Through "diffusing," other activities are destroyed. By "balancing," the wind and mind are gathered into the <term>Avadhuti</term> <gloss>central channel</gloss>. These are the limits of the three actions. At various times of the "piercing" of water, if an impurity or leak is encountered, nothing will be accomplished and destruction will follow. Through the two types of "diffusing," sickness will arise. Through "balancing," the preparation of elixirs and medications will be accomplished. Fire and wind together destroy the aggregates. Through "diffusing," all activities are accomplished, and through "balancing," the ends of mistaken activities are reached. In water and fire, the purpose is perfectly accomplished. Through "diffusing," one enters into others. Through "balancing," life and power are accomplished. In earth and wind, pacification is accomplished. Through "diffusing," enrichment and suppression are performed. Through "balancing," wrathful activities are accomplished. The activities of wind and water degrade. Through "diffusing," all virtuous activities are accomplished. Through "balancing," one is victorious in battle. Earth and fire are accomplished through "increasing." Through "diffusing," the existing elements are accomplished. Through "balancing," the rituals of strength are accomplished. Through diffusing...

<leaf-break/>

...and the Nirmanakaya <note>emanation body</note> will certainly be accomplished. The sound of earth is cool and heavy; it possesses the melodic voice of Great Brahma. If one always listens to and practices this, the Sambhogakaya <note>enjoyment body</note> will certainly be accomplished. The sound of fire is long and undulating; it shows the melodic speech of Great Vishnu. Whoever practices listening to this will certainly obtain the qualities of the Dharmakaya <note>truth body</note>. The sound of wind is piercing and fierce; it is the yoga-speech of the King of Birds <note>Garuda</note>. If one knows how to recite this always, one should train in the commonality of the Body and Speech. Thus, the meaning of the sounds of the four elements should be applied with certainty to the external times. The flow of spring, summer, and autumn are linked to water, earth, fire, and wind. If these are applied with certainty to the times and synchronized with the yogi's body, there is no doubt they will be accomplished. Regarding the limits of common worldly activities: those who wish to fly rely on pills. Those who wish for invisibility should settle the mind; by placing both body and mind within the web of the "Empty Bindu" <note>original: "thig le stong pa"</note>, it is accomplished. Those who wish to obtain "Unimpeded Penetration" <note>original: "zang thal"</note> should hold the wind itself and dwell in the Bindu. Occasionally, when the consciousness is like a mist, it should be ejected from the "Opening of Brahma" <note>at the crown of the head</note>. Those who wish to be victorious over weapons and poison should focus the mind on the four elements; by purifying the later elements and practicing well, these will certainly be accomplished. To be victorious over dogs, bears, and wolves, one should vocalize the four elements; by performing the four dependent-links, one will be victorious over them. Those who wish to be liberated from the "eight fears" should hold a "hare-marked" disk <note>the moon</note> at the crown and meditate on the wind; this too will bring victory over them. Those who wish to accomplish "Eye-medicine" <note>original: "mig pun"</note> should use a paper preparation called "Khati." If it is well-prepared and the "Letters of Illumination" are constantly recited, even the three realms will appear clearly. Those who wish to be victorious in war, trade, or marriage should grasp the time and direction of the elements; if this is done without error, there is no doubt of success. Whatever...

<leaf-break/>

...develops the experience. By the "Light Experience" <note>original: "la ba'i nyams"</note> of one's own system, if one becomes familiar with it, even the Heruka will be accomplished. The "Scent of Wind" is the place of training. One should combine the natural state with activity; if one meditates clearly on the sequence of the "Certain Gathering," the Kayas of the Five Families will certainly be accomplished. Furthermore, by training in the sequence of the "One and Two Tastes," whatever Kaya one desires will be accomplished without a doubt. Whoever meditates on the "Yoga of Sleep" uses ignorance as the path. Regarding the "External Time": one should train the yogi's body in its skills from the <unclear>kha dag</unclear> <gloss>primordial purity</gloss> state; the key point is to exhaust the channels internally. Regarding the "Internal Time": by the natural state itself, one should train the yogi's speech in its skills; the key point is to cut the flow of expression. Regarding the "Secret Time" of the four: one should train the yogi's mind in its skills; the key point is familiarity with sleep. Through the four "Times of Reality" <note>original: "kho na nyid kྱི་དུས་"</note>, one definitely gathers the body, speech, and mind and mixes sleep with the Great Clear Light. If the yogi is familiar with this, they will certainly be joined to the Three Kayas. Regarding taking the key points of the Dream as the path: first, perform the preliminaries and strike the vital points. Preliminarily, based on the signs of having trained the body, speech, and mind, one should definitely grasp the three: "permanence," "overwhelming with brilliance," and "latent tendencies." Then, at the time of striking the vital points, through the points of "purifying," "causing," "cutting," "stirring," "extracting the essence," and "leaving it at the vital point," and through the "reversal of the mandala," the dreams of karma are exhausted, and the confusion of latent tendencies is uprooted and cast away. At this time, through one's own diligence, the best will know the channels and the intermediate will know the activities. The certain outcome is that they will be transformed; these are the many initial dreams. For the best, the "forgotten speech" is finally blocked. For the intermediate, it is very clear. For the lowest, it becomes clear through conservation and then transforms. These reach the standard. When a person's own mind does not overflow, and one meditates on non-conceptuality, it will certainly overflow; when it settles into its natural state, that is one's own ground. The sequence of previous training and the four actualities rely on their own causes...

After that, the <term>Dakini</term> <gloss>sky-goer</gloss> <term>Palzinma</term> will hold this very doctrine, and it will flourish during the time of the ten-year lifespan. Then, it will not remain, returning to its own ground. This heart-essence of the doctrine...

<leaf-break/>

...will be. Thus, one cannot finish describing it; the end of the doctrine is inconceivable. For a moment, it is indicated by words. As for the body and branches of the Tantra: within the body, there are two hundred and fifty sections. First, through the certain clarity of the Various Array instructions, regarding the seventy questions, the Instructions Array consists of one hundred sections. This completes the body itself. Its branches are six hundred and ten. The higher body and branches are completed. The body-completing instructions are the secret-makers. The second body is shown: in the Array of the Gathering Places, for the twenty-eight questions, the Gathering Places Array consists of thirty-one sections. By that, the body itself is completed. The branches are two hundred and one hundred <note>three hundred</note>. By those, the second body and its branches are completed. The third body is supported: for the twenty-two questions, the Wisdom Array consists of fifty-eight sections. For the branches themselves, there are two hundred. The third body and branches are completed. The fourth body and branches: the questions are twenty-one, and the Reality Array consists of thirty-two sections. The branches are sixty-four. For the fifth body and branches: the questions are eleven, and the View and Meditation Array consists of thirty-two sections. Its branches are sixty-four. The fifth body and branches are completed. The sixth body and branches: written for the eight questions, the Kayas Array consists of eighteen sections. Its branches are thirty-two. The sixth body and branches are completed. The desires of the elements are as follows: from the specific karmas of the crown and common actions, the support-ground for the karma of sentient beings is based on the external elements. Thus, karma, nourishment, the faculties, the retinue, and birth are asserted as complete. The order of the internal elements and karma: the earth element constitutes the four parts of the body; through its creation, it is asserted as the ripening of the earth element. By fire, the entire body is generated; through its creation, it is asserted as the ripening of heat. By wind, the entire body is lifted; through its creation, it is asserted as the ripening of breath. The specific meanings of those sounds...

<leaf-break/>

...first arrayed. From the first formless levels of the inner heights, the realms of form and the Clear Light arise. In the desire realm as well, through the stainless moon and the clearly illuminating sun, the world-realms spread. There are four stages of the higher levels such as "Emanating Others' Creations." Then come the abodes of the <term>Asuras</term> <gloss>demi-gods</gloss>, followed by the stages of the four continents. Along with the ego of the afflictions, the abodes of the lower realms are formed in stages. Within the migration of the six classes of beings, they are formed internally, and their body size, lifespan, and activities are many due to karma. The respective abodes and merits are situated in accordance with the continents. The meaning concerns destruction, formation, abiding, and emptiness; birth, aging, illness, and death; and the very cycle of existence. The shifting of time is as follows: from the initial "incalculable" time until the final "ten-year" period, there is upward growth and downward waning. Through the three minor eons of disease, famine, and weapons, after sixty stages have passed, seven destructions by fire and seven by water occur. In this way, after fourteen are completed, the remainder is destruction by wind. The abiding in sixty stages and the duration of destruction are the same; it remains empty for sixty stages. Thus, a hundred and a hundred and ten are asserted as the first duration of an eon. Thus, one hundred and eighty is the second intermediate eon. Such a duration is called one Great Eon. Thirty days make one month. The completion of twelve such months is asserted as one year. Seven hundred mornings and evenings, when the days are complete, are asserted as three hundred and sixty days. By completing these, one year is formed; the days are distinguished by the activities of male and female. The months of autumn, spring, summer, and winter—each with three full moons—perform the tasks of entering and speaking. The rat, ox, tiger, hare, snake, dragon, horse, sheep, monkey, bird, and...

<summary>This page details the lineage of the Great Perfection (Dzogchen) teachings from primordial Buddhas to historical masters like Garab Dorje and Vimalamitra. It also categorizes the structural components of the Tantras and explains the cosmological formation of world-realms, lifespans, and the cyclical destruction of the universe by the elements.</summary>

...the pig; these twelve spread the calculations of the elements. For increasing life, healing, accomplishment, and the rites of kings, if a <term>Yogi</term> knows the application, they will become equal to the sun and moon. Furthermore, if a <term>Yogi</term> knows how to manipulate the activities of diminishing, destroying, summoning, binding, striking the vital points, transferring, and killing, all beings will be brought under their power. Increasing and healing the "power-capacity" <note>original: "dbang thang"</note>, and the acts of stabilizing or breaking—other practices of diminishment—should be undertaken by the <term>Yogi</term>. There are twelve movements, dispersals, and balances: three for each of the four elements of earth, water, fire, and wind. By the movement of water, the faculties are gathered. By its dispersal, they are disturbed. By its balance, results are produced. By the movement of earth, dust is produced. By its dispersal, the limbs are held. By its balance, the arising of the body is completed. By the movement of fire, illness is caused. By its dispersal, the state of the body is changed. By its balance, the elements are stabilized. By the movement of wind, the elements are protected. By its dispersal, other activities are destroyed. By its balance, the wind and mind are gathered in the <term>garu</term> <note>central point</note>. These are the limits of the three functions. At certain times of the water movement, by meeting the leaking of the essence, nothing will be accomplished and things will be destroyed. By the two dispersals, illness occurs. By balance, the compounding of elixirs and medicines is accomplished. By fire and wind, the aggregates are destroyed. By dispersal, all activities are accomplished. By balance, the activities of delusion reach their end. With water and fire, the purpose is excellently accomplished. By dispersal, one enters into others. By balance, life and power-capacity are accomplished. With earth and wind, pacification is accomplished. By dispersal, enrichment and submission are performed. By balance, the activities of wrathful magic <note>original: "mngon spyོད་"</note> are accomplished. The tasks of wind and water are diminished. By dispersal, all virtuous activities are accomplished. By balance, one is victorious in battle. Earth and fire are accomplished by increasing. By dispersal, existing elements are accomplished. By balance, the ritual of physical strength is accomplished. By dispersal...

<leaf-break/>

...the <term>Nirmanakaya</term> <gloss>Emanation Body</gloss> will also certainly be accomplished. The sound of the earth is cool and heavy; it possesses the melodic voice of Great Brahma. If one always listens to and practices this, the <term>Sambhogakaya</term> <gloss>Enjoyment Body</gloss> will certainly be accomplished. The sound of fire is long and waving; it shows the melodic resonance of Great <term>Vishnu</term>. Whoever practices listening to this will certainly obtain the qualities of the <term>Dharmakaya</term> <gloss>Truth Body</gloss>. The sound of wind is piercing and fierce; it is the applied speech of the King of Birds <note>Garuda</note>. If one knows how to recite this always, one will train in the commonality of Body and Speech. Thus, the meanings of the sounds of the four elements are certainly applied to the external time. Throughout the sequence of spring, summer, and autumn, through water, earth, fire, and wind, the times are certainly applied in order; if this is made to harmonize with the <term>Yogi's</term> body, there is no doubt of accomplishment. As for the limits of common worldly activities: those desiring flight rely on pills. Those desiring invisibility rest the mind; by placing both body and mind within the web of the empty <term>bindu</term> <gloss>essence-drop</gloss>, it is accomplished. Those desiring to obtain unimpeded transparency hold the wind itself and reside in the <term>bindu</term>. When awareness is known at times to be like a mist, it should be extracted from the aperture of Brahma. For those desiring to be victorious over weapons and poisons, the mind is focused on the four elements; by practicing well to purify the latter, those will certainly be accomplished. To be victorious over dogs, bears, and wolves, one recites the four elements; by making the four dependent connections, one will be victorious over them. For those desiring to be freed from the eight fears, hold the wheel-drawing itself at the crown of the head and meditate on the wind; then one will also be victorious over those. For those desiring to achieve "eye-medicine" <note>original: "mig pun"</note>, by properly combining the substance called <term>Kati</term> and paper, and constantly reciting the clarifying syllables, even the three realms will appear clearly. For those desiring to be victorious in war, trade, or marriage, by seizing the time and direction of the elements and acting without error, there is no doubt they will certainly succeed. Whatever...

<leaf-break/>

...experience is generated. By the experience of the earth in one's own system, if one becomes familiar with it, even <term>Heruka</term> will be accomplished. The scent of the wind is the place of training; by combining it with the activities of the mode of abiding, if one meditates clearly on the sequence of certain gathering, the five families and their bodies will certainly be accomplished. Furthermore, regarding taste and the two touches, by training in the sequence accordingly, there is no doubt that whatever body one desires will be accomplished. Whoever meditates on the <term>Yoga</term> of sleep, this makes the path of ignorance. Regarding the external time, the skill of the <term>Yogi's</term> body is trained from the openings, and it is vital to exhaust the channels internally. Regarding the internal time, through the natural state itself, the skill of the <term>Yogi's</term> speech is trained, and it is vital to cut the stream of expressions. Regarding the secret time, through the four also, the skill of the <term>Yogi's</term> mind is trained, and familiarity with sleep is the vital point. Through the four times of suchness, the body, speech, and mind are certainly gathered, and the Great Clear Light is mixed with sleep. By thus becoming familiar, the <term>Yogi</term> is certainly joined to the three <term>Kayas</term>. If one takes the vital point of dreams as the path, first perform the preliminaries and strike the vital points. First, regarding body, speech, and mind, based on the signs of mastery, one must certainly seize the three: permanence, overwhelming brilliance, and habitual tendencies. Then, at the time of striking the vital point, through purifying, transforming, cutting, agitating, extracting the essence, and leaving it at the vital point, the vital point of the reversal of the center is performed. Thus the ten karmic dreams are exhausted, and the delusions of habitual tendencies are uprooted and discarded. At this time, through one's own diligence, the best is known from the channels, the middling from the results, and the lowest is certain to change; these are the many initial dreams. For the best, the forgotten speech is finally stopped; for the middling, it is very clear; for the lowest, it is clarified with effort and then changes. These arrive at the measure of the result. When the individual's own mind has not overshot, and is certainly overshot by meditating on non-conceptuality, when it arrives at rest, that is one's own ground. The sequence of previous training and the four actualities depend on their own causes...

<summary>This page describes various yogic practices related to the four elements, including methods for worldly power, protection from fears, and the attainment of the three Buddha-bodies. It specifically details the Yoga of Sleep and Dream Yoga, explaining how to transform ignorance and habitual tendencies into the Clear Light and non-conceptual awareness.</summary>
<keywords>Yoga, Elements, Sleep, Dream Yoga, Kayas, Bindu, Clear Light, Siddhi, Diligence, Non-conceptuality</keywords>
