<translation page="8">
The Good One took hold in the abode of the Array of the Dense. Then, in the abode of Alakāvatī, he took hold of this very Sarvavid Vairochana and matured into the five families. Beyond that, through my own holding, the teachings are completed and perfected. The one thousand and two Buddhas surely emerge based on this. Beings born through transformation, from eggs, from warmth, and from the womb are matured. From this very teaching of the Discipline, the twelve wheels of Dharma emerge. His thirty-six deeds, based on Body, Speech, and Mind, were granted to the beings who were the objects of training. After I pass into Nirvāṇa, in the country of Oḍḍiyāna to the west, there will be the noble lady of Dhanakośa; without a father, a son will be born, Vajrapāṇi <note>original: "Badzra Pune te"</note>. He will hold the sacred teachings. His successor in the western direction will be the fortunate Brahmin boy named Mañjushrīmitra <note>original: "Man dzu bri pra ti"</note>; he will hold them for seventy-five years. After him, a fortunate one in the land of Sosadvīpa <note>original: "Sho sha'i gling"</note> from a householder family, named Shri Singha, will be the holder. After him, the holder from a Chāṇḍāla <note>original: "gdol pa"</note> family, Jñānasūtra, will hold this very thing. After him, the holder from a householder family, Vimalamitra <note>original: "Phyag dya dya chen"</note> will hold them. After him, one from a royal family, the Emanation Body together with his attendants, will hold them. After him, in the form of a renunciant, Lhun gyi Gyaltsen. After that, Simhashvara will hold them. After that, the Bodhisattvas dwelling on the stages will hold them. Below that, the emanation of Vajrapāṇi, Vajraphala, will hold them. After that, King Sengge the Good will be the holder. Below that, the scholar Palzin. Below that, the yogi Phrawa will hold them. Below that, King Thri Ö. Below that, the monks Pal and Yön. Then, Lodrö Chog will hold them. Beyond that, the Dakini Palzinma, having held this very teaching, will cause it to flourish during the time of the ten-year lifespan. Then, it will not remain but return to its own place. This Heart-Essence of the teachings...

<leaf-break/>

...will become. In that way, it is more than can be expressed; the end of the teachings is inconceivable. For now, it is illustrated with words. As for the body and branches of the Tantra, in the body there are two hundred and fifty arrays. First, through the certain clarity, in the miscellaneous instructions of the array, for the seventy requested topics, there are one hundred and one instructional arrays. The body itself is thus completed. Its branches are six hundred and ten. The bodies and branches of the higher ones are completed; the body is completed and the instructions are kept secret. The second body is shown as follows: in the array of the gathered abodes, for the twenty-eight requested topics, there are thirty-one arrays of gathered abodes. By that, the body itself is completed; the branches are two hundred and eighty. By that, the second body and the branches are completed. The third body is supported as follows: for the twenty-two requested topics, there are fifty-eight arrays of wisdom. For the branches themselves, there are two hundred. The third body and branches are completed. The fourth body and branches: the requested topics are twenty-one, and there are thirty-two arrays of the nature of phenomena. The branches are sixty-four. For the fifth body and branches: the requested topics are eleven; there are thirty-two arrays of view and meditation. Its branches are sixty-four. The fifth body and branches are completed. The sixth body and branches: for the eight written requested topics, there are eighteen arrays of the Kayas. Its branches are thirty-two. The sixth body and branches are completed. The desire of the elements is as follows: from the specific activities of the supreme pinnacle, the ground which is the support for the karma of beings, based on the outer elements, it is held that karma, nourishment, the faculties, the retinue, and birth are completed. As for the sequence of karma of the inner elements: by earth, the four of the body are made; through its generation, it is held to be the maturation of the earth element. By fire, the whole body is generated; through its generation, it is held to be the maturation into warmth. By wind, the whole body is supported; through its generation, it is held to be the maturation into breath. Its specific meanings of the sounds...

<leaf-break/>

...arranged first. From the first formless inner heights, the realms of form and the Clear Light; then in the desire realm, from the stainless moon and the intensely illuminating sun, the world realms spread; after that come the higher stages such as the Emanation of Others, then the abodes of the demi-gods, and the beings of the four continents in sequence. Along with the self of the afflictions, the abodes of the lower realms are sequentially formed. Among the beings of the six classes, they are formed within; the size of the body and the length of the lifespan are many due to their specific karma. The respective abodes and merits are situated in accordance with the continents. The meaning is destruction and formation, abiding and emptiness, birth, aging, sickness, and death; it is the very cycle of existence. The transition of time is as follows: from the beginningless infinite time down to the final ten-year age, there is upward growth and downward decline. Through sickness, famine, and weapons—the three minor kalpas—the transition is made. After sixty have passed, there are seven by fire and seven by water <note>Wait, "seven by water" might be an error for another number in some systems, but it reads "chu mi bdun" here</note>. When fourteen are thus completed, the remainder is the destruction by wind. In that way, the duration of abiding for sixty and the duration of destruction are of that same amount; for sixty, it remains empty. In that way, one hundred and one hundred and ten is held to be the duration of the first kalpa. In that way, one hundred and eighty is the second intermediate kalpa. That which is proclaimed as that much is one great kalpa. For thirty days, there is one month; when twelve of these are completed, it is held to be one year. When seven hundred morning and evenings and the days are completed, it is held to be three hundred and sixty days. By completing these, the year is formed; the days are distinguished by the karma of male and female. The months of autumn, spring, summer, and winter; each one is entered by three full moons, and they perform the activities of speech. The Rat, Ox, and Tiger; the Hare, Snake, and Dragon; the Horse, Sheep, and Monkey; the Bird and...
</translation>

<translation page="9">
...and the Pig; by these twelve, the calculations of the elements are increased. Increasing and healing life, and the rituals of achievement and kingship; if the yogi knows the application, he will become equal to the sun and moon. Others include degrading, destroying, summoning, binding, and striking the vital points. Also the activities of shifting and killing; if the yogi knows the disruption, beings will be brought under control. Increasing and healing power, and the acts of staying and breaking; the application for the degradation of others should be undertaken by the yogi. There are twelve of scattering, piercing, and leveling: for earth, water, fire, and wind, these four each have three, making twelve. Through the piercing of water, the faculties are gathered. Through scattering, they are agitated. Through leveling, the fruit is brought forth. Through the piercing of earth, the atoms are brought forth. Through scattering, the branches are held. Through leveling, the arising of the body is completed. Through the piercing of fire, sickness is caused. Through scattering, the state of the body is changed. Through leveling, the elements are made to abide. Through the piercing of wind, the elements are protected. Through scattering, other activities are destroyed. Through leveling, the wind and mind are gathered into the "ga". This is the limit of the three actions. Regarding the piercing of water at various times: by the meeting of the leakages <note>original: "zhag pa zag pa"</note>, whatever is not accomplished will be destroyed. Through the two scatterings, sickness occurs. Through leveling, the compounding of elixirs and the like are accomplished. Through fire and wind, the aggregates are destroyed. Through scattering, all activities are accomplished. Through leveling, the activities of delusion reach their end. In water and fire, the purpose is perfectly accomplished. Through scattering, one enters into others. Through leveling, life and power are accomplished. Through earth and wind, pacification is accomplished. Through scattering, enrichment and suppression are performed. Through leveling, the activities of direct action <note>term: mngon spyod gloss: wrathful activities or sorcery</note> are accomplished. Through wind and water, activities decline. Through scattering, all virtuous activities are accomplished. Through leveling, one is victorious in war. Through earth and fire, increase is accomplished. Through scattering, the existing elements are accomplished. Through leveling, the ritual of power is accomplished. Through scattering...

<leaf-break/>

...the Emanation Body is also surely accomplished. The sound of earth is cool and heavy; it possesses the melodic sound of Great Brahma. If one always practices listening to this, the Complete Enjoyment Body is surely accomplished. The sound of fire is far-reaching and surging; it shows the melodic voice of Great Vishnu. Whoever practices listening to this will surely obtain the qualities of the Dharma Body. The sound of wind is piercing and fierce; it is the applied speech of the King of Garudas. If one knows how to chant this always, one should train in the commonality of Body and Speech. In that way, the meaning of the sounds of the four elements is surely applied to the outer time. As for the continuity of spring, summer, and autumn: by water, earth, fire, and wind, they are sequentially and surely applied to the times. If they are made to harmonize with the body of the yogi, there is no doubt they will be accomplished. As for the common mundane results: those desiring flight should rely on pills. Those desiring invisibility should settle the mind; by placing both body and mind within the web of the empty bindu, it is accomplished. Those desiring to obtain transparency should hold the wind itself and enter the bindu. When the consciousness occasionally becomes like mist, it should be extracted from the Brahma-opening. Those desiring to be victorious over weapons and poison should focus the mind on the four elements; after practicing well to purify the latter, those things will surely be accomplished. To be victorious over dogs, bears, and wolves, one should vocalize the four elements; having made the four interdependent connections, one will be victorious over them. Those desiring to be freed from the eight fears should hold the mountain-shaped wheel on the crown; if they meditate on the wind, they will also be victorious over those. Those desiring to accomplish the "clouded-eye" <note>unclear: mig pun</note> should properly combine the paper-mixture called *khati*; if the clear-making syllables are always chanted, even the three realms will appear as clarity. In war, trade, and marriage, those who desire to be victorious should seize the time and direction of the elements; even if they act without delusion, there is no doubt it will be accomplished. Whatever...

<leaf-break/>

...experience is generated. By the experience of the path of one's own system, if one becomes familiar, even Heruka is accomplished. The scent of the wind is the place of training; the natural mode should be combined with activities. If one meditates clearly on the sequence of certain gathering, the body of the five families will surely be accomplished. Furthermore, by training in the sequence of the two flavors and so on, there is no doubt that whatever Kayas one desires will be accomplished. Whoever meditates on the yoga of sleep, by this, takes ignorance as the path. Regarding the outer time, from the gates: one should train the strength of the body of the yogi, and the key point is to consume the channels within. Regarding the inner time, through the very nature: one should train the strength of the speech of the yogi, and the key point is to cut the continuity of expression. Regarding the secret time, through the four: one should train the strength of the mind of the yogi, and the key point is familiarity with sleep. Through the four times of suchness: having surely gathered the body, speech, and mind, one mixes sleep with the Great Clear Light. Having become familiar in that way, the yogi surely joins with the three Kayas. Regarding the taking of the key point of dreams as the path: first one should perform the preliminaries and strike the key points. For the preliminaries of body, speech, and mind: based on the signs of mastery, one should surely seize the three: permanence, overwhelming, and karmic tendencies. Then, at the time of striking the key points: through purifying, transforming, cutting, agitating, extracting the essence, and leaving at the key point. By performing the key point of reversing the center, the ten karmic dreams are exhausted, and the delusion of karmic tendencies is pulled out and discarded. At this time, through one's own diligence, the best is known from the channels, the middling from the... <note>original: "rtsa dang 'bring las shes"</note>, and the least is certain to change; for these, the first dreams are many. For the best, the forgotten speech is finally stopped. For the middling, there is extreme clarity; then the least is protected and clear and then changes. Through those, the measure is reached. If the man's own mind has not overstepped, it surely oversteps through meditating on non-conceptuality; when it returns to its natural state, it is one's own ground. The sequence of previous purification and the four actualities depend on their own causes...
</translation>

<summary>This page describes a lineage of Dzogchen masters, the structural layout of the tantra's "bodies" and "branches," and technical instructions for elemental yogas, worldly accomplishments, and the yogas of sleep and dreams.</summary>
<keywords>lineage, Vairochana, Mañjushrīmitra, Shri Singha, Jñānasūtra, Vimalamitra, tantra structure, elemental yoga, sleep yoga, dream yoga, clear light, bindu, accomplishments</keywords>

Among the beings of the six classes, they are formed within; the size of the body and the length of the lifespan are many due to their specific karma. The respective abodes and merits are situated in accordance with the continents. The meaning is destruction and formation, abiding and emptiness, birth, aging, sickness, and death; it is the very cycle of existence. The transition of time is as follows: from the beginningless infinite time down to the final ten-year age, there is upward growth and downward decline. Through sickness, famine, and weapons—the three minor kalpas—the transition is made. After sixty have passed, there are seven by fire and seven by water <note>Wait, "seven by water" might be an error for another number in some systems, but it reads "chu mi bdun" here</note>. When fourteen are thus completed, the remainder is the destruction by wind. In that way, the duration of abiding for sixty and the duration of destruction are of that same amount; for sixty, it remains empty. In that way, one hundred and one hundred and ten is held to be the duration of the first kalpa. In that way, one hundred and eighty is the second intermediate kalpa. That which is proclaimed as that much is one great kalpa. For thirty days, there is one month; when twelve of these are completed, it is held to be one year. When seven hundred morning and evenings and the days are completed, it is held to be three hundred and sixty days. By completing these, the year is formed; the days are distinguished by the karma of male and female. The months of autumn, spring, summer, and winter; each one is entered by three full moons, and they perform the activities of speech. The Rat, Ox, and Tiger; the Hare, Snake, and Dragon; the Horse, Sheep, and Monkey; the Bird and...

...and the Pig; by these twelve, the calculations of the elements are increased. Increasing and healing life, and the rituals of achievement and kingship; if the yogi knows the application, he will become equal to the sun and moon. Others include degrading, destroying, summoning, binding, and striking the vital points. Also the activities of shifting and killing; if the yogi knows the disruption, beings will be brought under control. Increasing and healing power, and the acts of staying and breaking; the application for the degradation of others should be undertaken by the yogi. There are twelve of scattering, piercing, and leveling: for earth, water, fire, and wind, these four each have three, making twelve. Through the piercing of water, the faculties are gathered. Through scattering, they are agitated. Through leveling, the fruit is brought forth. Through the piercing of earth, the atoms are brought forth. Through scattering, the branches are held. Through leveling, the arising of the body is completed. Through the piercing of fire, sickness is caused. Through scattering, the state of the body is changed. Through leveling, the elements are made to abide. Through the piercing of wind, the elements are protected. Through scattering, other activities are destroyed. Through leveling, the wind and mind are gathered into the "ga". This is the limit of the three actions. Regarding the piercing of water at various times: by the meeting of the leakages <note>original: "zhag pa zag pa"</note>, whatever is not accomplished will be destroyed. Through the two scatterings, sickness occurs. Through leveling, the compounding of elixirs and the like are accomplished. Through fire and wind, the aggregates are destroyed. Through scattering, all activities are accomplished. Through leveling, the activities of delusion reach their end. In water and fire, the purpose is perfectly accomplished. Through scattering, one enters into others. Through leveling, life and power are accomplished. Through earth and wind, pacification is accomplished. Through scattering, enrichment and suppression are performed. Through leveling, the activities of direct action <note>term: mngon spyod gloss: wrathful activities or sorcery</note> are accomplished. Through wind and water, activities decline. Through scattering, all virtuous activities are accomplished. Through leveling, one is victorious in war. Through earth and fire, increase is accomplished. Through scattering, the existing elements are accomplished. Through leveling, the ritual of power is accomplished. Through scattering...

<leaf-break/>

...the Emanation Body is also surely accomplished. The sound of earth is cool and heavy; it possesses the melodic sound of Great Brahma. If one always practices listening to this, the Complete Enjoyment Body is surely accomplished. The sound of fire is far-reaching and surging; it shows the melodic voice of Great Vishnu. Whoever practices listening to this will surely obtain the qualities of the Dharma Body. The sound of wind is piercing and fierce; it is the applied speech of the King of Garudas. If one knows how to chant this always, one should train in the commonality of Body and Speech. In that way, the meaning of the sounds of the four elements is surely applied to the outer time. As for the continuity of spring, summer, and autumn: by water, earth, fire, and wind, they are sequentially and surely applied to the times. If they are made to harmonize with the body of the yogi, there is no doubt they will be accomplished. As for the common mundane results: those desiring flight should rely on pills. Those desiring invisibility should settle the mind; by placing both body and mind within the web of the empty bindu, it is accomplished. Those desiring to obtain transparency should hold the wind itself and enter the bindu. When the consciousness occasionally becomes like mist, it should be extracted from the Brahma-opening. Those desiring to be victorious over weapons and poison should focus the mind on the four elements; after practicing well to purify the latter, those things will surely be accomplished. To be victorious over dogs, bears, and wolves, one should vocalize the four elements; having made the four interdependent connections, one will be victorious over them. Those desiring to be freed from the eight fears should hold the mountain-shaped wheel on the crown; if they meditate on the wind, they will also be victorious over those. Those desiring to accomplish the "clouded-eye" <note>unclear: mig pun</note> should properly combine the paper-mixture called *khati*; if the clear-making syllables are always chanted, even the three realms will appear as clarity. In war, trade, and marriage, those who desire to be victorious should seize the time and direction of the elements; even if they act without delusion, there is no doubt it will be accomplished. Whatever...

<leaf-break/>

...experience is generated. By the experience of the path of one's own system, if one becomes familiar, even Heruka is accomplished. The scent of the wind is the place of training; the natural mode should be combined with activities. If one meditates clearly on the sequence of certain gathering, the body of the five families will surely be accomplished. Furthermore, by training in the sequence of the two flavors and so on, there is no doubt that whatever Kayas one desires will be accomplished. Whoever meditates on the yoga of sleep, by this, takes ignorance as the path. Regarding the outer time, from the gates: one should train the strength of the body of the yogi, and the key point is to consume the channels within. Regarding the inner time, through the very nature: one should train the strength of the speech of the yogi, and the key point is to cut the continuity of expression. Regarding the secret time, through the four: one should train the strength of the mind of the yogi, and the key point is familiarity with sleep. Through the four times of suchness: having surely gathered the body, speech, and mind, one mixes sleep with the Great Clear Light. Having become familiar in that way, the yogi surely joins with the three Kayas. Regarding the taking of the key point of dreams as the path: first one should perform the preliminaries and strike the key points. For the preliminaries of body, speech, and mind: based on the signs of mastery, one should surely seize the three: permanence, overwhelming, and karmic tendencies. Then, at the time of striking the key points: through purifying, transforming, cutting, agitating, extracting the essence, and leaving at the key point. By performing the key point of reversing the center, the ten karmic dreams are exhausted, and the delusion of karmic tendencies is pulled out and discarded. At this time, through one's own diligence, the best is known from the channels, the middling from the... <note>original: "rtsa dang 'bring las shes"</note>, and the least is certain to change; for these, the first dreams are many. For the best, the forgotten speech is finally stopped. For the middling, there is extreme clarity; then the least is protected and clear and then changes. Through those, the measure is reached. If the man's own mind has not overstepped, it surely oversteps through meditating on non-conceptuality; when it returns to its natural state, it is one's own ground. The sequence of previous purification and the four actualities depend on their own causes...

Treat by seeking out the specific foods and medicines that counteract the condition. Regarding the transformation of chronic indigestion into other diseases: because it originally arises from the cause of indigestion, change the "Five Pomegranates" formula by adding "King Salt" and white sugar. Giving boiled water will generate the digestive fire of the stomach. This clears the site of indigestion and leaves the clear essence in its own place. It becomes an easy friend to the other resulting diseases. To treat the result without treating the cause is like removing only the poison from milk while the water remains sour. Because all internal diseases are produced by indigestion, it is extremely important to treat the indigestion first. If the cause itself is released, how can the result occur? So it was said. <leaf-break/>

...is in the lungs, heart, liver, gallbladder, spleen, and kidneys. Bile, stomach, large intestine, small intestine, and the lower abdomen. Blood tumors occur in the liver, spleen, stomach, and large intestine. Bile tumors occur in the gallbladder and small intestine. Vessel tumors occur in the lungs, kidneys, liver, and "vessel-loops" of the small intestine. Hair tumors stay in the stomach, large intestine, small intestine, and gallbladder. Parasite tumors occur within both the stomach and large intestine. Water tumors are not fixed and can occur anywhere, but are common between the lungs, heart, liver, and intestines. <term>Sbag</term> tumors <note>a type of spreading tumor</note> arise and pulse without a fixed location. Briefly, there are three: external, internal, and intermediate tumors. External tumors are between the outer skin of the organs and the flesh. Intermediate tumors are on the inner walls of the hollow organs or sides of the solid organs. Disease tumors stay in the depths of all solid and hollow organs. As for how they form: through hard food, fat, and accumulated dregs. Indigestion does not clear on its own and turns into mucus. Indigestion of the waste becomes a "food tumor." Through the condition of indigestion, Phlegm and mucus increase. By the constriction of Wind, it becomes what is called a <term>lhen</term> tumor. Undigested clear essence in the stomach <unclear>...</unclear>
</translation>

By repeatedly accumulating and ripening into hardness, it becomes what is called a "Stone tumor" of undigested clear essence. Indigestion in the liver causes bad blood to collect. Droplets of blood form at the bottom of the liver. By increasing and collecting, it becomes a "Blood tumor" of the liver. When that falls into the small intestine, it mixes with Bile. When such a thing enters the spleen, it is a "Spleen tumor." When liver blood falls into the stomach, it churns with Phlegm. When constricted by blood and heat, it becomes a "Brown Phlegm tumor." When that enters the "pierced" large intestine, it becomes a "Large Intestine tumor." When that falls into the small intestine, it mixes with Bile; by being constricted into hardness, it becomes a "Bile tumor of the small intestine." Indigestion in the liver falls into the gallbladder. When Bile forms a coating and constricts, it is a "Gallbladder tumor." When indigestion and bad blood collect, they travel through the vessels of the liver-knife, lungs, kidneys, small intestine-loops, and stomach; by constricting in one place, they become "Vessel tumors." Blood stagnant from weapons <note>trauma</note> is the same. Indigestion travels to the vessel-pores of the lower abdomen. By being cooked by the heat of the water <note>bodily fluids</note>, it constricts into a stone-like shape. In women <unclear>...</unclear>
</translation>

<summary>These pages detail specific treatments for various types of indigestion based on the food source and describe the progression of chronic indigestion into complex abdominal tumors (lcong-nad). The text categorizes these tumors by their physical location and the elemental humors (Wind, Bile, Phlegm) involved in their formation.</summary>

From the <term>bha-ga</term> <gloss>source of phenomena</gloss>, emanate the assembly of the mandala gates. From the Great Supreme Primary Deity <note>Chechok Heruka</note>, father and mother, emanate the ten tamers of the proud directional guardians. From Vajra Heruka, father and mother, emanate the eight great <term>Gauri</term> <gloss>female deities of the cemetery</gloss>. From Manjushri Yamantaka, father and mother, emanate the twelve directional guardians with their retinues. From Padma Wangchen <note>Hayagriva</note>, father and mother, emanate the eight great wrathful Overpowering Ones. From Vajra Kilaya, father and mother, emanate the ten terrifying wrathful males with their wrathful females. From the Unsurpassed Heruka, father and mother, come the fourteen Queens of Wisdom. From the Union of All Proud Ones, father and mother, come the eight classes of Great Powerful Proud Ones. From the Mighty Black One, father and mother, come the eight classes of wrathful spirits surrounded by their retinues. From the Accomplished Vajra Holder come the eight types of Accomplished Knowledge Holders <note>Vidyadharas</note>. In the outer courtyard are the twenty-eight <term>Ishvari</term> <gloss>powerful goddesses</gloss>. Upon the outer encircling iron mountain are the <term>Dakinis</term>, <term>Gings</term>, and <term>Lankas</term>, the mothers and sisters, the flaming ones and the messengers, and the vast hundreds of thousands of Dakinis who are the natural attendants of the Glorious Command.

Thus, having clearly generated the essence, bless the body, speech, and mind. Grant empowerment through the five wisdoms. Invite the deities from their natural abode and perform the offerings, praises, and entrustment of activity. Alternatively, remain in the state of the <term>dharmata</term> <gloss>intrinsic nature</gloss> itself, the unconditioned self-clarity. For whoever enters and has devotion for this authentic path, they will be joined to the spontaneously accomplished stage. There is no doubt that this is achieved in a single lifetime. Thus it was said.

like a reflection in a mirror, they appear yet are indeterminate and individually distinct. Whoever meditates in that way will engage with the entire ocean of enlightened activity. <translation page="9">
Doubt regarding existence and non-existence was severed. Because the request was made, certainty was found. Therefore, the result became manifest. Furthermore, listen to the heart of the assembly! In the realm without edge or center, the Buddha <term>Namkhai Nyingpo</term> <gloss>Essence of Space</gloss> shows the teachings of the effortless result to the circles of faithful listeners. After circumambulating him with ultimate faith, an <term>utpala</term> <gloss>blue lotus</gloss> flower was offered as a support for requesting the definitive meaning. The request for the definitive meaning was this: "In the essence of natural purity, where no appearances exist in the ground, how did the sudden deluded appearances arise?" As soon as that was asked, the Buddha <term>Namkhai Nyingpo</term> was pleased by the <term>utpala</term> flower and spoke this answer to the request: "The ground is like space, without appearances. Through the condition of ignorance and the act of subject-object grasping, because of one's own deluded attachment to appearances, the appearances of habitual tendencies arose like clouds." By saying that, doubt regarding whether appearances exist or not was severed. Because the request was made, there is no lack of certainty. Therefore, the result became manifest. Furthermore, listen to the heart of the assembly! In the realm of expanding qualities, the Buddha known as <term>Bumzik</term> <gloss>Beholding a Hundred Thousand</gloss> shows the teachings of the effortless result to his own circles of faithful listeners. After circumambulating him with complete conviction and faith, a golden-colored lotus was offered as a support for requesting the definitive meaning. When the definitive meaning was requested from him, by means of the inseparable continuous <term>samadhi</term> <gloss>meditative absorption</gloss>, the awareness—

<leaf-break/>

—that intention. For the sake of realizing through symbols for those who have not realized it after meditating on the words, go as you see fit. When thus encouraged, all the <term>vidyadharas</term> <gloss>knowledge-holders</gloss> offered their thoughts and replied with great gratitude: "The command of the Lord of Devas is very kind; may the faithful people of Jambudvipa <note>the human world</note> clear away the darkness of ignorance. May the <term>Sugatas</term> <gloss>ones gone to bliss</gloss> grant their blessing." When that was said, the great <term>vidyadhara</term>, the Lord of Devas, became very pleased, and the Lord of Devas made this promise: "To the disciples who are suitable vessels for the definitive meaning, if I am able to explain this great tantra of the secret definitive meaning without alteration or corruption, may the assembly of <term>Sugatas</term> grant their blessing." After making that pledge, he said: "Furthermore, listen to the heart of the assembly!" Then the Son of the Devas thought: "Humans lack clairvoyance and miraculous powers. Therefore, I will explain this to the suitable vessels among the humans of Jambudvipa." Thinking this, he sought a support for his emanated birth. There was a woman of neither noble nor low birth, the <term>yakshini</term> <gloss>nature spirit</gloss> <term>Kunsopa Changchubma</term> <gloss>Enlightened Provider for All</gloss>. Intending to be born from her, he emanated as a bird with a golden body, silver wings, iron claws, turquoise eyebrows, a <term>vajra</term> <gloss>adamantine</gloss> beak, and precious eyes. At the break of dawn as the sun rose, the bird appeared in the sun's rays, touched its beak to the heart of <term>Changchubma</term>, dissolved into her heart, and remained for three days. A small boy was formed—
</translation>

<translation page="10">
—there is no inner or outer; what need is there for the coming of formal meditation and post-meditation? Having heard the meaning of that request, the Buddha <term>Bumzik</term> who was residing there was pleased by the golden lotus and spoke this answer to the request: "In this very wisdom-awareness, formal meditation and post-meditation have never existed from the beginning. For a meditator who lacks this definitive meaning, post-meditation arises in the mind of the five gates <note>the five senses</note>." By saying that, doubt regarding formal meditation and post-meditation was severed. Because the request was made, certainty was found. Therefore, wisdom became manifest. Then, that joyful <term>vidyadhara</term> remembered his former place and went to the Cave of Precious Manifest Joy in the eastern direction of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three. Because he remained in non-conceptual <term>samadhi</term> within, for the sake of the benefit of all sentient beings, he went before the Lord of Devas, <term>Indra</term>, and encouraged the Son of the Devas with these words: "You are an emanation of <term>Shakyamuni</term>, without equal in the three worlds. All the teachings of the Buddha are perfected in your mind. To the suitable vessels of Jambudvipa in the desire realm, speak the dharma that is realized merely by being shown, in well-composed verses." When thus encouraged, the Son of the Devas replied: "Since this great tantra of the secret definitive meaning is clearer than one's own mind but does not fall into words, it is very difficult for me to explain." When he had said that, understanding the necessary purpose, the Lord of Devas requested the meaning: "For the sake of future faithful ones, the authentic definitive meaning—

<leaf-break/>

—possessing the Lord. Having been born <unclear>near her</unclear>, he spoke these words: "All phenomena are the naturally arisen primordial wisdom. Cyclic existence is ignorance from the very beginning. The essence is not produced by causes or conditions. One's own awareness is the <term>dharmakaya</term> <gloss>truth body</gloss>." When one who proclaimed such things appeared, he was a wonder in this world. He was even given the name <term>Garab Dorje</term> <gloss>Supreme Joyous Vajra</gloss>. Possessing the five branches of knowledge and the qualities, he mastered the six clairvoyances simultaneously. He was seen to be honored by all people. Invited by his qualities, he was requested to reside in the Place of Bliss. At that time, while the emanation <term>Garab</term> remained continuously and inseparably in the intention of internal <term>samadhi</term>, the <term>yakshas</term> and demons were provoked. To create obstacles, the four Maras <note>personifications of death and delusion</note> performed acts of threatening and seducing. Knowing them to be the demons of the gods, he did not lose mindfulness even in a daze. For the sake of compassion, he relaxed his <term>samadhi</term>. Not being deceived by both seduction and threats, the demons were discouraged and overwhelmed. To express their sorrow, they sought refuge: "Look upon us with great compassion! Through the karma of ignorance, we were born as <term>rakshasas</term> <gloss>demonic spirits</gloss>. we ate the bodies and lives of sentient beings as food. We repent our evil karma in our hearts and will protect your teachings. We will consume the bodies and lives of those who break their vows. I offer this, the essence of my life, so do not let your compassion be small." After thus seeking refuge, they offered the essence of their own lives to the great <term>vidyadhara</term> <term>Garab</term> and vowed to protect the teachings.
</translation>

<summary>
These pages recount the transmission of the definitive meaning through various Buddhas and the miraculous birth and life of the master Garab Dorje. It highlights the resolution of doubts concerning the nature of reality and the vow of spirits to protect the secret teachings.
</summary>

<keywords>
Garab Dorje, Namkhai Nyingpo, Bumzik, samadhi, definitive meaning, Jambudvipa, vidyadhara, demons, protection of teachings
</keywords>

Having heard the meaning of that request, that Buddha <term>Bumzik</term> who was presiding was pleased in his heart by the golden lotus and spoke this answer to the request: "In this very <term>rigpa</term> <gloss>gnostic awareness</gloss> of primordial wisdom, meditative equipoise and post-meditation have never existed from the beginning. For a meditator who lacks this definitive meaning, post-meditation occurs in the mind of the five gates <note>the five senses</note>." By saying that, doubts about meditative equipoise and post-meditation were cut away. Because the request was made, certainty was found. Therefore, primordial wisdom became manifest. Then, that <term>Vidyadhara Semga</term> recollected his former state and went to the Cave of Precious Manifest Joy in the eastern direction of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three. By sitting in non-conceptual meditative equipoise within, for the sake of all sentient beings, he went before <term>Indra</term>, the Lord of Devas, and urged the Son of the Devas thus: "You are an emanation of <term>Shakyamuni</term>; you have no rival in the three worlds. All the Buddha's teachings are perfected in your heart. For the sake of the vessels in the human world of the Desire Realm, speak the Dharma that is realized just by being taught, in words of excellent composition." When he had been so urged, the Son of the Lord of Devas replied: "Since this great secret Tantra of definitive meaning is clearer than one's own mind, it cannot be reduced to words; therefore, it is very difficult for me to explain it." When he had spoken thus, the Lord of Devas understood the necessary purpose and requested the meaning: "For the sake of the faithful ones of future generations, the authentic definitive meaning..."

<leaf-break/>

...<term>rje can</term> <note>fragment of a name, likely Garab Dorje</note>. Having been born from the <unclear>rtsar</unclear>, he spoke these words: "All dharmas are self-arisen primordial wisdom. <term>Samsara</term> is ignorance from the very beginning. The essence is not produced by causes or conditions. One's own <term>rigpa</term> is the <term>Dharmakaya</term> <gloss>Truth Body</gloss>." After such a proclamation occurred, he was a wonder in this world. He was given the name <term>Garab Dorje</term>. Possessing the five sciences of qualities, he knew the six clairvoyances all at once. He was seen to be honored by all people. Being invited by his manual qualities, he was requested to reside in the Place of Bliss. At that time, that emanation <term>Garab</term>, while his heart remained continuously and inseparably in the enlightened intent of inner <term>samadhi</term>, was provoked by the <term>Yakshas</term> and <term>Maras</term>. For the sake of creating obstacles, the four "destroyers" performed acts of threatening and seduction. By knowing them to be the <term>Maras</term> of the devas, he did not lose mindfulness in the midst of the <unclear>mya ma myo</unclear>. For the sake of compassion, he relaxed his <term>samadhi</term>. Not being deceived by both the seduction and the threats, the <term>Maras</term> were disheartened and overwhelmed. To bring forth their mourning, they requested refuge: "Look upon me with great compassion! Due to the karma of ignorance, I was born as a <term>Rakshasa</term>. I have eaten the bodies and lives of sentient beings as food. I repent my evil karma with my mind. I will protect your teachings. I will eat the bodies and lives of those who break their vows. I offer this, the essence of my life; do not let your compassion be small!" Having thus requested refuge, he offered the essence of his own life to the great <term>vidyadhara</term> <term>Garab</term> and [pledged] to protect the teachings.

By saying that, doubt regarding meditative absorption and subsequent attainment was severed. Because the request was made, certainty was found. Therefore, wisdom was manifested. Then, that <term>Vidyadhara</term> <term>Semga</term> <gloss>Joyous Mind</gloss> remembered his former place and went to the cave of <term>Rinchen Ngonga</term> <gloss>Precious Manifest Joy</gloss> in the eastern direction of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three. Because he sat in absorption without results within, he went before <term>Sakra</term>, the Lord of Devas, for the sake of all sentient beings and exhorted the son of the gods as follows: "You are an emanation of <term>Shakyamuni</term>, without rival in the three worlds. All the teachings of the Buddha are perfected in your mind. For the sake of the suitable vessels in the desire realm of <term>Jambudvipa</term>, speak the Dharma that is realized just by being shown, in words of excellent composition." When thus exhorted, the son of the Lord of Devas replied: "Because this great secret tantra of definitive meaning is clear from one's own mind but does not translate into words, it is extremely difficult for me to explain." When he had said that, the Lord of Devas understood the necessary meaning and requested the point for the sake of the faithful of future generations, the authentic definitive meaning...

<leaf-break/>

...possessed of <term>vajra</term>. Born from the womb <note>original: "rtsar gyis" likely a corruption for "bstsal gyis" or related to birth</note>, he spoke these words: "All phenomena are primordial self-arisen wisdom. Cyclic existence is ignorance from the very beginning. The essence is not produced by causes or conditions. One's own awareness is the <term>Dharmakaya</term> <gloss>Truth Body</gloss>." After one who proclaimed such things appeared, a wonder in this world, he was given the name <term>Garab Dorje</term>. Possessing the five sciences of qualities, he knew the six clairvoyances all at once. He was seen to be honored by all people. Invited by the hand of qualities, he was requested to reside in the Place of Bliss. At that time, that emanation <term>Garab</term> remained with his mind continuously and inseparably within the intention of meditative absorption. Consequently, the <term>Mara</term> <gloss>demon</gloss> of the <term>Yakshas</term> committed provocations; for the sake of creating obstacles, the four "ruiners" <note>the four Maras</note> performed acts of threatening and seduction. By knowing them to be the Maras of the gods, his memory did not fail in the midst of the delusions. For the sake of compassion, he relaxed his meditative absorption. When he was not deceived by either the seductions or the threats, the Mara was overwhelmed with despair. To remove his anguish, he sought refuge: "Look upon me with great compassion. Through the karma of ignorance I was born as a <term>Rakshasa</term> <gloss>demon</gloss>. I ate the bodies and lives of sentient beings as food. I repent my evil karma with my heart. I will protect your teachings. I will eat the bodies and lives of those who break their vows. I offer this, the essence of my life; do not let your compassion be small." Having thus sought refuge, he offered the essence of his own life to the great <term>Vidyadhara</term> <term>Garab</term> and vowed to protect the teachings...
</translation>

<summary>These pages detail the transmission of the "Great Secret Tantra of Definitive Meaning" through various Buddhas and the Lord of Devas, Sakra. It describes the miraculous birth of the master Garab Dorje as an emanation to teach humans and his subsequent subduing of demonic forces that attempted to obstruct his meditation.</summary>

<meta>continues from previous page</meta>and even if the head is cut off in every way, the perception of happiness will remain present. There will be no arising of any perception that is neither happy nor unhappy. Why is that? Because this <term>Bodhisattva Mahasattva</term> <gloss>Great Heroic Being of Awakening</gloss> has for a long time, while practicing the conduct, made this aspiration: "May those who have given me food obtain the happiness of pacification. May those who have given me drink, and those who have performed service for me, and those who have honored, respected, and made offerings to me, all obtain the happiness of pacification. Even those who abuse me, cause me unhappiness, strike me, hit me with weapons, and do everything up to taking my life—may they all obtain the happiness of enlightenment and awaken into unsurpassed, perfect, and complete Buddhahood." Having made such aspirations and possessing those mental engagements, and through such karma and aspirations, they show, attend to, meditate on, and increase the perception of happiness that follows all sentient beings. From the ripening of that, they find happiness in all phenomena.
<leaf-break/>
All those who obtain the realization <note>of the dharma</note> are under the power of the <term>Tathagata</term> <gloss>Thus-Gone One</gloss>. Then, the gods of the <term>Shubhakritsna</term> <gloss>Vast Virtue</gloss> realm, having spoken this <term>samadhi</term> <gloss>meditative absorption</gloss>, at that time praised the Blessed One with these verses: 

"All these hosts of <term>Shubhakritsna</term> gods have reached the limit of phenomena. I take refuge with my head bowed to the Teacher, whose senses are peaceful and who knows peace. These wise ones worship the Buddha who knows the ultimate meaning and has crossed the ocean of cyclic existence. I praise the Leader of Men, the <term>Muni</term> <gloss>Sage</gloss> who is skilled in the way of leading, the Victorious One who leads the leaders. 

In this world, there is no permanent essence to the Sage's Dharma; just as a magician knows his illusions, you, O Sage, well understand them. Just as a wise man understands the various echoes arising in the mountain range, so you, the <term>Sugata</term> <gloss>One Gone to Bliss</gloss>, the <term>Rishi</term> <gloss>Seer</gloss>, behold the world with its gods and men. 

In this world, there are no sentient beings, no life-force, no nourished soul, and no person. You, the best of men, have dismantled perceptions and established the state of emptiness. O supreme among bipeds, chief of sentient beings, you also practice the meditation on immeasurable loving-kindness. This intention of the Victorious Buddha is difficult for all beings to realize. The Leader has taught that the cultivation of the virtue of loving-kindness has sentient beings as its object."

<summary>This page describes a Bodhisattva's profound aspiration to bring all beings, whether they help or harm him, to the happiness of enlightenment. It also contains verses from the Subhakrtsna deities praising the Buddha's realization of emptiness and his immeasurable compassion.</summary>
<keywords>Bodhisattva, aspiration, enlightenment, Subhakrtsna gods, emptiness, Loving-kindness, Samsara, Tathagata</keywords>

...guided, so that even if his head is cut off in every possible way, the perception of happiness will remain present. Furthermore, perceptions of neither happiness nor unhappiness will arise at all. Why is that? It is because this <term>Bodhisattva Mahasattva</term> <gloss>Great Heroic Being of Awakening</gloss> has for a long time, while practicing the conduct, made the following aspiration: "May all those who have given me food obtain the happiness of complete peace. May all those who have given me drink, and all those who have rendered me service, honor, respect, and offerings, all obtain the happiness of complete peace. Furthermore, may all those who revile me, make me unhappy, strike me, wound me with weapons, and even those who go so far as to take my life in every possible way, all obtain the happiness of awakening and realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment." Having made such an aspiration, he possesses those mental engagements. Because he possesses such actions and such aspirations, he demonstrates, relies upon, meditates on, and cultivates the perception of happiness that follows after all sentient beings. Through the maturation of that, he is happy regarding all phenomena.

The wise ones who worship the Buddha, the Knower of the Meaning who has crossed over cyclic existence, praise the Leader of leaders, the Victorious One who is skilled in the manner of the Sage, the guide of men. Here, there is no abiding in the Dharma of a Sage that has a fixed inherent nature; just as a magician knows an illusion, you, O Sage, understand it well. Just as the wise realize that various sounds are like echoes arising in the mountain ranges, so do you, <term>Sugata</term> <gloss>One Gone to Bliss</gloss>, the Great Seer, view the world including the gods and men. Here, there are no sentient beings, no life-force, no nourished soul, and no person. You, Supreme among Men, have dismantled perceptions and established them in emptiness. You, the Best of Bipeds, the Foremost of Beings, also practice the meditation on immeasurable loving-kindness. This intention of the Victorious Buddha is difficult for all wandering beings to realize. The Leader has declared that the cultivation of the virtue of loving-kindness has sentient beings as its object."

Since there are many connections. In that case, these, which are like connections of an unceasing nature, are both; however, for others, it is uncertain. If it is shown that by performing the <term>mchod brjod</term> <gloss>verses of worship</gloss>, others are produced, then who are those others? If one asks how they arise from the worship, here there are two types: those of dull faculties and those of sharp faculties. 

Regarding the first: those who enter primarily through the individual person, or who follow faith where conviction arises from mere words, develop clarity. The nature of this clarity is "thorough," meaning it is great. "For a moment" refers to the order of explanation, or that this arises more quickly than in those of sharp faculties. The object is this <term>Yum</term> <gloss>Mother/Prajnaparamita</gloss>. Regarding the manner: by showing the Mother as possessing the previously explained qualities, clarity arises quickly because it occurs immediately upon hearing the words, without investigation or doubt as to whether she truly possesses such qualities. Regarding the cause: through the verse beginning with "Hearers etc.," the three qualities of greatness—whereby this Mother produces the aims of the four sons—are stated to be superior to those of outsiders, Hearers, Solitary Realizers, and Bodhisattvas. Clarity arises based on hearing that statement.

Regarding the second: not only those of dull faculties, but also those who follow the Dharma by entering primarily through the teaching, or by entering after investigating the meaning, also develop clarity; this is how the connection is made. The nature of this clarity is "thorough," meaning it is irreversible. Toward what? Toward that Mother. Here, the use of "that" <note>referring to something distant</note> and "this" <note>referring to something near</note> relates to the proximity within the worship verses. The "ornament" is as before. As for the manner: is it merely through the sutra's statement that the Mother produces the four sons? No, it is not. Generally, while the cause for the dull-facultied to engage or turn away is mere words, those of sharp faculties investigate whether there is logical contradiction.

<leaf-break/>

There is no need to hold onto a proof just to avoid a loss of status. In this context, it is not as if the dull-facultied, failing to see whether there is contradiction, simply hold the statement that the Mother produces sons to be true. Rather, one must explain that after investigating whether there is contradiction, and seeing no contradiction, they hold that she produces the sons. Therefore, it is incorrect for those two texts to contradict each other. 

Regarding the second text: because it appears as the <term>bsgrub bya</term> <gloss>the thing to be proven</gloss>, it is incorrect to take it as the <term>sgrub byed</term> <gloss>the proof</gloss>. Well then, what is the proof? As explained before, when the display of the worship and the Madhyamaka reasonings appear to conflict, one investigates. If, upon investigation, one sees that the two are not in conflict, clarity arises. Therefore, what is the use of holding onto another's proof? 

The second point is also incorrect. Investigating whether there is logical contradiction applies to what is explicitly stated in the words of the worship. There, the Mother producing sons is explicitly stated, whereas the non-arising of the three bases and paths is not explicitly stated. 

In the <term>Tshig gsal</term> <gloss>Clear Words / Prasannapada</gloss>, the subject is <term>Sher phyin</term> <gloss>Perfection of Wisdom</gloss>. The specific qualities are the three knowledges. The reason for showing them as three is to refute the idea that they are indistinguishable even in relative truth, and to show how the three sons are greatly produced. For it is praised: "Of the Buddhas, you are the Mother. You are the sole path of liberation followed with certainty by the Hearers. There is no other." Thus, if this Mother possessed a realization superior to the individual realizations of the respective vehicles, and if this sutra which teaches it had nothing superior to other sutras, then the part of this that produces Hearers and Solitary Realizers would be the mere realization of the selflessness of persons, and the part that produces Bodhisattvas and Buddhas would be the realization of the two selflessnesses. If one thinks these were taught respectively in the <term>Dran pa nyer bzhag</term> <gloss>Applications of Mindfulness</gloss> and the <term>Sdong po bkod pa</term> <gloss>Gandavyuha Sutra</gloss>, then to clear that up, it says "possessing the three modes."

<leaf-break/>

It would follow that there is nothing except for the Mother, and yet the Mother is not the path for these individuals. Such a wish is impossible. The two signs are cited from the scriptural praise as evidence and are accepted by the two basic schools of tenets. If one asserts that the <term>gzhi shes</term> <gloss>knowledge of bases</gloss> and <term>lam shes</term> <gloss>knowledge of paths</gloss> are exclusively the Mother of Buddhas, then the two persons taught as Hearers and Bodhisattvas would also become merely nominal. 

Therefore, this kind of explanation, which gathers many contradictions, is a mockery of both Maitreya and the Master <note>likely Haribhadra</note>. Those who follow this have also failed to investigate well. For that reason, regarding the meaning of the "way it was made a basis for error," it is explained in accordance with the thought "intending to establish the three modes," as the <term>bum pa</term> <gloss>Vessel/Lower vehicles</gloss> desiring the three modes of the vehicles, or as the three modes of dividing the three knowledges. 

If one argues: "The Master also asserts that the sutra paths are nominal Perfections of Wisdom, so there is no disagreement, since the Perfection of Wisdom and the Mother are one in meaning," this is most incorrect. The meaning of "Mother" is simply the fulfillment of the unique aims of the four sons; how can the Master say this does not exist for Hearers and Solitary Realizers? Furthermore, since they would lack a Mother with defining characteristics, the sons would also become merely nominal. 

By saying "The division into three knowledges is not a division of different natures" and "Though appearing as many, the essence is only one," the position of the <term>Tshig gsal</term> <gloss>Clear Words</gloss>—which asserts that while the Mother of Bodhisattvas has defining characteristics, the Mother of Hearers does not—is refuted. This is because he asserts the Mother of Buddhas alone as being one with the Knowledge of All Modes <note>Sarvakarajñata</note> possessing defining characteristics. Enough of this elaboration. 

Regarding the second: it is said, "In order to engage with the meaning." If one asks how they engage: they act with devotion. Where? In that Mother whose qualities lead to the pacification of...

<leaf-break/>
...it would become so; because there is nothing except the Mother, and the Mother is not the path for these. One cannot accept that. Therefore, an explanation like this, which gathers many contradictions, is a mockery of both Maitreya and the Master <note>likely Haribhadra</note>, and those who follow this have not investigated well. Therefore, even the meaning of the "manner of the basis of error" is explained in accordance with the thought that "it is intended as the arrangement of the three modes," as the "three modes of the vehicles" which the *Hundred Thousand Verse* version desires, or as the "three modes of the division into three knowledges." Enough of this elaboration. Regarding the second: if it is said "in order to engage with the meaning," how does one engage? One acts with respect. Where? If it is shown that "by making the praise" others and "generation" <note>the generation of realizations</note>, then who are the "others," and how is it "from the praise"? To this, there are two:
the disposition of those with dull faculties and those with sharp faculties. Regarding the first: those who enter by focusing primarily on the individual, or who follow faith where conviction arises from mere words, develop clarity. The essence is "greatly," meaning "to a high degree." "For a while" refers to the order of explanation, or that for these, the first <note>stage of clarity</note> arises more quickly than for those of sharp faculties.
The object is this Mother <term>Prajnaparamita</term> <gloss>Perfection of Wisdom</gloss>. The manner is that by showing the Mother to be endowed with the previously explained qualities, it arises immediately upon hearing the words without investigation and without doubting whether she possesses such qualities or not; thus it is "quickly." The cause is expressed by this verse beginning with "Hearers etc." <note>referring to a standard verse of praise</note>, stating that she possesses the three qualities of the greatness of having produced the aims of the four sons, which are superior to those of outsiders <note>non-Buddhists</note>, Hearers, Solitary Realizers, and Bodhisattvas. It is by relying on hearing that expression. Second: not only for those of dull faculties, but it should also be applied to those who follow the Dharma, entering by focusing primarily on the teaching or by entering after investigating the meaning, that she also "causes clarity to be produced." The essence of clarity is "greatly," meaning "irreversible." Regarding what? Regarding that Mother. Here, "that" and the "this" above refer to the proximity or distance within the praise.
The ornament is as before. As for the manner: is it then only regarding the Sutra's teaching that "the Mother produced the four sons"? No, it is not. While the cause for the engagement or withdrawal of those with dull faculties is mere words, those with sharp faculties, when investigating whether there is contradiction by reasoning, find no contradiction and...

<leaf-break/>

...there is no need to hold a proof that [it] does not decline. Here, when those of dull faculties are clear, it is not like holding the teaching that the Mother produced the sons to be true without seeing whether there is contradiction or not; rather, when investigating whether there is contradiction, they see it is without contradiction and then hold that she produced the sons. Since this explanation is required, it is incorrect for those two texts to be in contradiction. Regarding the second text: because multiple objects of proof appear, it is incorrect to hold them as the proof. Then, what is the holding of the proof? As explained before, when one who is not clear investigates the presentation of the praise and the Madhyamaka reasonings which appear to be in conflict, they see that the two are not in conflict, and clarity arises; therefore, what is the use of holding the proofs of others? The second is also incorrect: investigating whether there is contradiction by reasoning applies to what is explicitly stated in the words of the praise. There, the "Mother producing the sons" is explicitly stated, while the "non-arising of the three bases and paths" is not explicitly stated. In the *Clear Words* <note>the commentary Prasannapada</note>, the subject is the Perfection of Wisdom. The distinction is the three knowledges. Showing them as three is to refute the thought that they are indistinguishable even in relative truth, and to show how the three sons are greatly produced. For it is praised: "Of the Buddhas... O Mother of the Buddhas! / You are the single path to liberation / surely relied upon by the Hearers; / there is no other," and so forth. If that is so, then the realization of this Mother would be superior to the realizations of the individual vehicles, and this Sutra which teaches it would also have nothing superior to other Sutras. If one thinks that the part of this which produces Hearers and Solitary Realizers is merely the realization of the selflessness of the person, while the part which produces Bodhisattvas and Buddhas is the realization of the two selflessnesses—and that these are taught respectively in the *Applications of Mindfulness* and the *Gandavyuha*—then to clear that up, it says, "possessing the three modes"...

<leaf-break/>

...it would become; for there is nothing except the Mother, and yet the Mother is not the path for these. One cannot accept [that], and the two signs are cited from the scriptural authority of the praise as the evidence, and are accepted by the two basic philosophical systems. If one asserts the Knowledge of Bases and the Knowledge of Paths to be the Mother of the Buddhas alone, then the two types of individuals taught as Hearers and Bodhisattvas would also become merely nominal. Therefore, an explanation like this, where many contradictions converge, is a mockery of both Maitreya and the Master <note>Haribhadra</note>, and those who follow this have also not investigated well. Therefore, even the meaning of the "manner of making it a basis for error" is explained in accordance with the phrase "intending to establish the three modes," as the <term>Shatasahasrika</term> <gloss>The Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred Thousand Lines</gloss> desiring the "three modes of the vehicle," or else as the "three modes of dividing into three knowledges." If it is said: "Even the Master asserts the texts and paths to be nominal Perfections of Wisdom, so there is no disagreement, because the Perfection of Wisdom and the Mother are one in meaning," this is most incorrect. The meaning of "Mother" is merely to accomplish the unique desired aims of the four sons; how can the Master say that this does not exist for the Hearers and Solitary Realizers? Furthermore, since they would lack a definitive Mother, the "sons" would also become merely nominal. By the statement "The division into three knowledges is not a division of different natures; though appearing as many, the essence is only one," the view of the *Clear Words* is refuted—the view that while she is the definitive Mother of the Bodhisattvas, she is not for the Hearers—because it asserts her to be the definitive Mother of the Buddhas, being one with the Knowledge of All Aspects. Enough of this elaboration. Regarding the second: if it is said, "in order to cause engagement with the meaning," how does one engage? One acts with respect. Where? In the qualities of that Mother, such as leading to peace...
